surface.description:

call_id.description:

status.description:

Record per page fetched: the page's formats, as `page.formats` answers
them (its `url` the document's, after redirects), its response's
`status` and `fetched_at`, when the engine read it, and its named
`fields`, each read by a locator and given by a Value transform (ADR

is null, and the Record's Provenance names why (`unread_fields`);
none by default.

formats.description: The formats each page's Record holds, as `page.formats` takes them.

element whose link the Frontier would judge is not added, with
`link_limit`. None for no limit.

locator.description: The locator, on the page `crawl_request.handle` gave.

payload.description: The one Payload every link takes; never with `payloads`.

payloads.description:
Each matched element's own Payload, in the order
`crawl_request.links` answered them, as the program's Payload
function returned it: `null` skips that link, reported
`skipped_by_payload`. Never with `payload`.

priority.description:
Their priority among the requests of their domain, as
`crawl_request.enqueue`'s; 0 by default.

CrawlRequestEnqueueParams.description:
What `crawl_request.enqueue` takes: one request to add, from one attempt
of a crawl request.

body.description: The body it is sent with, if any.

crawl_request_id.description: The ID of the crawl request whose attempt enqueues.

document.description:
The document the handler read, whose base URL a relative `url`
resolves against; absent, the crawl request's own URL is the base.

forefront.description:
Whether it goes ahead of every request its domain holds pending,
whatever their priority, as Crawlee's `forefront` (ADR 0005): of two
such requests, the later goes first. A priority or `forefront` never
orders requests of different domains (ADR 0004); `false` by default.

key.description:
Its identity in the Frontier, declared by the program in place of
its method, its URL's key and its body's hash: a canonicalization
of the program's own, which always wins (ADR 0005).

lease_epoch.description: The attempt's lease epoch, as `crawl_request.handle` gave it.

method.description: The method it is sent with: `GET` by default.

payload.description: The data the program attaches for its handler.

priority.description:
Its priority among the requests of its domain: higher goes first; 0
by default.

url.description: The URL to add, absolute or relative to the document's base URL.

CrawlRequestHandleParams.description:
What `crawl_request.handle` gives the handler: one attempt of one work
item, under its lease.

lease_epoch.description: The lease's epoch, which only goes up (ADR 0003).

page_id.description:
The page served from the fetched document, which the handler reads
as any page; every request names one.

response.description:
The response of the request's own document, when the engine
fetched it: its final URL, status and headers as the site sent
them, the encoding its document was decoded with, and the
`request_id` whose body `response.body` reads (ADRs 0093 and 0119).
None when the browser's navigation answered none.

session.description: The Session of the crawl's Session pool that serves the attempt.

tier.description:
The tier that serves the request's page (`fetch.tier`): the engine
fetches every request's document, so every request names one.

CrawlRequestHandled.description:
What a handler answers once its attempt returned: the outputs it staged,
which commit once, under the attempt's lease (ADR 0003), or its skip.

records.description: The Records it pushed, in order.

skipped.description:
Its handler's skip: the request ends `skipped` with the reason
`handler`, and the attempt's Records are discarded.

CrawlRequestLinks.description:
What `crawl_request.links` answers: each element its locator matched,
in document order.

CrawlRequestLinksParams.description:
What `crawl_request.links` takes: the locator whose elements an
attempt's `enqueueLinks` reads before its Payload function runs.

crawl_request_id.description: The ID of the crawl request whose attempt reads the links.

lease_epoch.description: The attempt's lease epoch, as `crawl_request.handle` gave it.

locator.description: The locator, on the page `crawl_request.handle` gave.

CrawlRequestOutcome.description:
How one crawl request ended (ADRs 0079 and 0102). A request that
`run.retry_failed` re-admits ends again, and its later outcome
supersedes this one: a reader keys outcomes by `request.id`.

oneOf.description: Its handler returned, and what it staged was committed.

not_added.description:
Each request its attempt's enqueues, `enqueueLinks` calls and
seeds answered `added` that the commit did not add, in order.

nothing_committed.description: Why it committed no Record, when it committed none.

records.description:
Per Dataset its handler pushed into, the Records committed,
dropped and rejected.

oneOf.description: Its last attempt failed, and no retry is left.
A decision ended it.

message.description: The handler's or the Hook's own text.

reason.description: Why.

oneOf.description: The site refused it.

attempts.description: How many attempts it took: retries are a count, not an outcome.

errors.description: The error of each failed attempt, in order.

position.description:
Its place in the Run's commit order, from 1, which `run.outcomes`'s
`after` takes.

ended.description:
Whether the sequence is over: the Run has ended, or has no live
writer, and nothing committed after `next` matches.

next.description: The position the next page starts after.

outcomes.description: The outcomes that match, in commit order.

CrawlRequestPushParams.description:
What `crawl_request.push` takes: the Records of one push of an
attempt into one of its crawl's Datasets, one or several (ADR 0147).

crawl_request_id.description: The ID of the crawl request whose attempt pushes.

lease_epoch.description: The attempt's lease epoch, as `crawl_request.handle` gave it.

records.description:
The Records, at least one, in the order pushed: a Record's position
in this list is how `record_invalid` names it.

CrawlRequestPushed.description: What `crawl_request.push` answers once every Record is staged.

CrawlRunProgress.description:
A crawl's progress (ADR 0102): what a crawl adds to every Run's, a part
no area supplied being absent.

checkpoint_at.description: When its last Checkpoint was written, once one was.

concurrency.description: Its handlers running and the Resource governor's level.

epoch.description: Its run epoch (ADR 0003), which a resume or a migration advances.

idle.description:
Whether `crawl.keep_alive` holds it `running` with an empty Frontier
and nothing in flight, until `run.add_seed` gives it work.

in_flight.description: Each request being fetched or handled.

last.description:
Whether it is the sequence's last value: the Run ended, or no
engine this one reaches works it, so nothing more comes until a
start with its Run ID resumes it.

message.description: The program's own status line, once it set one.

position.description:
Its place among the Run's progress values, which only goes up:
`run.progress`'s `after` takes it.

stop_reason.description: Why it stopped, once it did.

storage.description:
The worst storage level among the filesystems the Run writes to,
once one is above `normal` (ADR 0122).

waiting.description: Why its due requests wait, one group per reason.

CrawlRunReport.description:
A crawl's Run report (ADR 0102): what a crawl adds to every Run's
report, a part no area supplied being absent. On the wire, a crawl's
parts sit beside every Run's, which a reader of [`RunReport`] keeps among
its `kind_parts`.

checkpoint.description: The last Checkpoint written of it in this engine, when one was.

completeness.description: Whether its results cover its scope.

completeness_reasons.description: Why it is not `complete`, when it is not.

error.description:
The error the call that ends it raises: the one that failed a
`failed` Run, or a write at its end that failed, such as its Plan
file's (ADR 0116).

nothing_done.description: Why the call that answered it did nothing, when it did nothing.

plan.description: What it did with its Plan file (ADR 0091).

policy_version.description:
The version of the Operator policy it ran under, when one applied
(ADR 0031).

recording.description: What it did with the Response recording its start named (ADR 0105).

settings.description:
Each effective value it ran with, the layer that set it and the one
that locked it, as `config.explain` gives them (ADR 0028).

sinks.description: Each Sink that applies to it (ADRs 0026 and 0103).

sitemaps.description: Each sitemap seed's sitemaps, as its progress gives them.

stop_reason.description: Why it stopped, when it did.

uncertain_effects.description:
Each Effect it left uncertain, until a person reconciles it (ADR
0106).

usage.description:
What it used, as the Usage ledger charged it, with the Limits that
apply to it (ADR 0101).

verdict.description: Whether its own checks prove what it committed.

verdict_reasons.description: Why it is not `verified`, when it is not.

warnings.description: What the areas warn of, each with a code and a message.

weakened.description: Every setting that weakened a safeguard for it (ADR 0028).

datasets.description:
The crawl's Datasets, each with its JSON Schema and its key (ADR
0103): a second of one name fails the start with
`dataset_duplicate`, and a key on a field the schema does not
require with `dataset_key_invalid`. Its handlers push Records only
into these.

detached.description:
Whether the Run outlives the Connection that started it (ADR 0102),
as a Recipe's run does: only a code-free crawl with no Hook, started
on a Daemon, detaches, and any other such start fails with
`detach_unsupported`.

extraction.description:
What a crawl with no handler reads from each page (a code-free
crawl, ADR 0103): the engine handles each request itself and
declares the Label and the Dataset it commits into, so such a start
declares no Dataset of its own, else it fails with
`invalid_params`. None for a crawl whose program handles its
requests.

hooks.description:
The crawl's Hooks in code, in the order declared (ADR 0104). Never
kept in the Run's state: a start that resumes the Run declares them
again.

labels.description:
The crawl's Labels, by name, each with its Payload's JSON Schema or
none, and its own settings (ADRs 0082 and 0093): a scope between the
Run and its requests. A Payload of a declared schema is checked
against it at every enqueue. A seed, a sitemap rule or an enqueue
naming a Label the crawl does not declare fails with
`label_unknown`, and so does a start under the ID of a Run with
pending requests of a Label no longer declared, before any work; a
code-free crawl declares its own Label.

limits.description:
The Run's own Limits, as `run.start` takes them (ADRs 0041 and
0080): at most one per Usage kind and currency. A start that names
the Run again lowers them and never raises them (ADR 0102).

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

run_id.description: The Run's ID, as `run.start` takes it.

seeds.description: The requests the crawl starts from.

settings.description: The Run's settings, nested by key: the run layer (ADR 0083).

CreditParams.description:
What `$/credit` grants: more events, or chunks, for a streaming call;
sent by the engine, more seeds a `run.add_seeds` call takes.

credits.description:
How many more events, or chunks, the Client takes; sent by the
engine, how many more seeds the call takes.

run_id.description: The Run ID of the run refused, when the call named one.

DaemonEndpoint.description:
Where a Daemon or an Attached engine's private endpoint listens (ADR
0024): a `0600` Unix socket on macOS and Linux, loopback TCP on
Windows.

oneOf.description: A Unix socket's path.
A loopback address and port.

DaemonHealth.description:
What `daemon.health` answers: what the ops listener's `/livez` and
`/readyz` check (ADR 0050). In a Daemon group, readiness ignores the
Lead Daemon's reachability.

live.description:
Whether it is live: its runtime and its Runs' registry, which writes
their run state, respond.

ready.description: Whether it is ready: live, and able to take a new Run.

unready.description: Why it is not ready, when it is not; empty when it is.

daemon.description:
What the Daemon answered, or `None` when no Daemon of the major
answered.

healthy.description: Its answer, which its exit code repeats: 0 when `true`.

DaemonState.description: What `daemon.status` answers: the running Daemon's state.

clients.description: How many Clients are connected, the caller included.

heap.description:
Its live heap: the bytes its own allocations hold now, as its
executable's allocator counts them, without the pages that
allocator keeps once they are freed; none where nothing counts
them.

kept_alive.description:
Whether it never stops idle: `--keep-alive`, a held Schedule or an
installed service.

live_runs.description: How many of its Runs are live.

product.description: The Product the Daemon runs as.

DaemonStatus.description:
What `daemon start`, `restart`, `stop`, `status`, `install` and `run`
print under `--json` (spec #608): the Daemon of the executable's major
that runs once the command is done, each field `None` but `major` when
none runs, as after `daemon stop`.

address.description: Where it listens: its socket's path, or `host:port`.

major.description: The executable's major, whose Daemon it is, such as `1` or `0.4`.

service.description:
The per-user service `daemon install` registered for the major;
absent when none is installed.

DaemonStopping.description: What `daemon.stop` answers, before the Daemon stops.

live_runs.description: How many live Runs it stops, each resumable from its own state.

removed.description: The service it removed, or `None` when none was installed.

fix.description:
What to do, such as starting the Daemon `GOODFETCH_URL` names or
checking `GOODFETCH_TOKEN`.

DatasetDeclaration.description:
One Dataset a crawl declares (ADR 0103): its name, the JSON Schema its
Records are checked against, and the top-level fields that identify one
Record.

key.description:
The top-level fields that identify one Record, each one the schema
requires; none when no field does.

name.description: Its name, unique in the crawl.

schema.description:
The JSON Schema its Records are checked against, the side the
program's schema parses from; none takes any JSON object (ADR 0082).

oneOf.description:
The key names a field that is no top-level field its schema
requires, as the Dataset is declared.

At a resume, the key of a Dataset that holds Records differs from
the one the Run began with.

began_with.description: The key the Run began with.

key.description: The key the crawl declares now.

datasets.description: Each Dataset the crawl declares, in the order declared.

next.description: The next page's `after`; absent once no Record follows.

records.description: The Records, in the page's order.

through.description:
The number of the last Record committed when the first page was
read: the next page's `through`.

after.description:
The number of the last Record of the previous page, its `next`: the
page starts after that Record in the page's order. Absent, at the
first.

columns.description: The top-level fields each Record's value keeps; absent, every one.

filter.description: Which Records to take; absent, every one.

limit.description: The most Records the page carries, from 1 to 1000; absent, 100.

through.description:
The previous page's `through`, so every page reads the Records
committed when the first was read. Absent, the last number
committed now.

limit.description:
The most rows it returns, at most `dataset.query.max_rows`; absent,
that setting's value.

runs.description: The runs it reads, from 1 to 100: only these are registered.

rows.description:
Its first rows, each a value per column as JSON, at most the
call's `limit`.

total.description: How many rows the query produced, those not returned counted.

DatasetRecord.description: One committed Record of a Dataset, as a reader reads it (ADR 0103).

number.description: Its number in its Dataset, from 1, in commit order, with no gaps.

provenance.description: How it was obtained (ADR 0123's Provenance of a Record).

request_id.description: The ID of the crawl request whose attempt committed it.

value.description: The Record, as JSON; the program's schema parses it.

DatasetRecords.description:
What a succeeded request's commit did with its Records in one Dataset
(ADR 0103).

rejected.description: How many the Dataset's schema rejected.

DatasetSummary.description: One Dataset a crawl declares, with what its crawl kept of it.

committed.description: How many Records the crawl committed into it.

dropped.description: How many a Hook dropped before their commit.

key.description: The top-level fields that identify one Record; empty when none do.

rejected.description: How many were rejected into its rejection table.

schema.description:
The JSON Schema its Records are checked against; none takes any
JSON object.

declared.description: The names of the Datasets the crawl declares, in order.

elapsed.description: How long the call waited, in milliseconds.

ended_by.description:
The enclosing call whose timeout ended it, when that call's end came
before its own (ADR 0080): `limit` is then that call's timeout.
Absent when its own timeout ended it.

limit.description:
The timeout's setting, its value in milliseconds and the layer that
set it.

observed.description:
The last state seen before it ended, such as a navigation under way
on its page, when the engine saw one.

waited_for.description: What it waited for, such as `first_byte` or `navigation`.

fix.description: How to start it detached, or how to start it without `detached`.

key.description:
What keeps the Run from detaching: `engine`, the Connection's
engine, which is no Daemon, or the key of the start that gives the
Run a handler in the program.

Dialog.description: A dialog as its handler sees it.

default_value.description: A prompt's default value; empty for any other kind.

DialogAcceptParams.description: What `dialog.accept` takes: the dialog, and a prompt's text.

prompt_text.description: The text a prompt returns; its default value when absent.

DialogAnswered.description: What an answer to a dialog answers once the page closed the dialog.

DialogHandleParams.description:
What `dialog.handle` gives the handler: the dialog, named by the ID its
answer passes.

dialog_id.description: The dialog, which an answer names.

id.description: The id of the `page.on_dialog` call whose handler is asked.

DialogHandled.description:
What the handler replies to `dialog.handle` once it ended; a failure
reply says it failed.

DialogId.description: One dialog a handler answers, which `dialog.*` names.

DialogType.description: A dialog's kind, as Playwright's `dialog.type()` names it.

oneOf.description: `alert()`.
`confirm()`.
`prompt()`.

A `beforeunload` handler that asks to stay: raised by a navigation,
or by `page.close` with `run_before_unload`.

DialogsEnded.description: What `page.on_dialog` answers when its page closes.

DoctorFinding.description: What `doctor` found about one part of the installation.

fix.description: What to do about it; present whenever the status is not `ok`.

message.description: What was found, for people; never matched on.

DoctorReport.description:
What `doctor --json` prints: its findings, in the order of
[`FindingId`].

findings.description: One finding for each part checked.

DownloadId.description:
A Download of a Run, named by the engine when it keeps its file:
`<run_id>.download-<position>`.

total_bytes.description: The bytes the answer announced, when it did.

path.description:
The program's path, absolute, which an Attached engine writes
itself; any other engine leaves it to the SDK and sends the file's
bytes instead.

DownloadSaved.description: What `download.save_as` answers once the file is whole.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, in lowercase hexadecimal.

written.description:
Whether the engine wrote the program's path itself; when not, the
`$/chunk` notifications before this answer carried every byte, and
the SDK writes the path.

operation.description:
The call that asked for the handlers, by its catalog name, such as
`crawl.start`.

runtime.description: The edge runtime the program runs on.

EdgeRuntime.description: The edge runtime a program runs on (ADR 0049), told by its marker.

oneOf.description:
Cloudflare Workers (`workerd`), whose `navigator.userAgent` is
`Cloudflare-Workers`.
Vercel's edge runtime, which sets the `EdgeRuntime` global.
Deno Deploy, whose environment holds `DENO_DEPLOYMENT_ID`.

EffectAttempt.description:
The crawl attempt an Effect is declared through: a handler's `ctx.run`,
which is bound to its attempt (ADR 0093).

crawl_request_id.description: The ID of the crawl request whose attempt declares the Effect.

lease_epoch.description: The attempt's lease epoch, as `crawl_request.handle` gave it.

EffectCloseParams.description:
What `effect.close` takes: the entry `effect.open` answered and how its
body ended.

run_id.description: The Run whose Effect journal keeps the Effect.

EffectClosed.description:
What `effect.close` answers: how the engine judged the body by what it
sent for it.

oneOf.description:
The body returned a value the Effect journal keeps: it never runs
again under its key, and the SDK answers `performed`.

The body did not return, and nothing was sent or the Effect is
repeatable: the entry is dropped, the SDK propagates the body's
error, and the next declaration runs the body.

sent.description: Whether something was sent for it.

oneOf.description:
The body did not return a value the Effect journal keeps after
something was sent, and the Effect is not repeatable: it never runs
again until a person reconciles it, and every later declaration of
its key raises `effect_uncertain`. The SDK raises `effect_uncertain`
with the body's error as its cause, or propagates a cut-short
body's error unchanged.

cause.description:
The Error code the body's value met, `effect_output_invalid`,
when it returned one the Effect journal does not keep.

effect.description: The Effect left uncertain, as the Run report lists it.

EffectOpenParams.description:
What `effect.open` takes: the Run, the Effect key and whether its body
is safe to run again.

attempt.description:
The crawl attempt whose handler's `ctx.run` declares the Effect
(ADR 0093), whose crawl request is the key's namespace. Absent, the
key's namespace is the Run.

key.description:
The Effect key, chosen by the program: 1 to 255 Unicode code
points. Its namespace is the crawl request in a handler and the Run
elsewhere.

repeatable.description:
Whether the body is safe to run again: a body that sent something
and did not return then runs again at its next declaration instead
of leaving its Effect uncertain. `false` by default.

run_id.description: The Run whose Effect journal keeps the Effect.

oneOf.description:
The Effect journal holds no answer: run the body, then
`effect.close` the entry.

entry.description: The Effect journal entry, which `effect.close` names.

idempotency_key.description:
An opaque key, the same on every attempt and resume of this
Effect on any machine and different in every Run and install,
for the body to send as a site's `Idempotency-Key`.

oneOf.description:
An earlier attempt or start performed the Effect: the body does not
run, and the output it returned then is the answer.

output.description: What the body returned, or absent when it returned nothing.

oneOf.description:
A person answered "it happened" (ADR 0029): the body does not run,
and no output is known.
It returned a value, or nothing.

output.description:
What it returned: JSON up to `effect.output.max_size` bytes, or
absent when it returned nothing.

oneOf.description:
It raised an error, which the SDK propagates, or wraps in
`effect_uncertain` when the Effect is left uncertain.

It was cut short: a cancellation or its attempt's end, whose error
the SDK propagates unchanged (ADRs 0080 and 0093).

address.description:
The address the connection would have used, when the rule judged
one.

setting.description:
The setting whose value would allow the request; none when no
setting would, as for a URL that does not parse.

url.description: The URL of the request refused, as the run gave it.

EgressRule.description: The rule of the egress policy that refused a request.

oneOf.description:
`egress.allowed_domains` does not list the host, or
`egress.blocked_domains` does, or the request could not be judged.
The address the connection would use is not globally reachable.
The URL's scheme is one no request may use.

ElementState.description: A state of the element a locator matches (Playwright's `waitFor`).

oneOf.description: One element matches.
No element matches.

One element matches, with a box of its own and `visibility:
visible`.
No element matches, or the one that does is not visible.

Email.description: An e-mail address the page shows.

text.description:
The text it was read from: its `mailto:` link's text, else the
address as the text writes it.

EnclosingCall.description:
The enclosing call a timeout belongs to, as `deadline_exceeded`'s
`ended_by` names it (ADR 0080): the calls made inside a call inherit its
end, so none outlasts it.

call_id.description: Its request's id on its Connection.

EncodingProvenance.description:
The encoding a Record's document was read in, and where it came from
(ADR 0119).

source.description:
Where it came from; none where the browser read the document by a
rule the engine did not see.

EncodingSource.description:
Where a document's encoding came from, in the order the tiers look
(ADR 0119).

oneOf.description: Its byte order mark.
`fetch.encoding`.
The `Content-Type` charset.
A declaration in its own bytes: a `<meta>` or an XML declaration.
Nothing declared, and the body is valid UTF-8.
The browser's guess, after the request escalated to it.

EndingError.description: An Error code a Run's ending raises, with its message and details.

EngineExitedDetails.description:
The evidence `engine_exited` carries of how the engine ended (ADR
0078). Each field is always sent: a linked engine, which runs in the
program's own process, has no exit code or signal, both `null`, and no
stderr of its own, an empty tail.

exit_code.description:
The engine's exit code; `null` when a signal ended it, or when it
is linked.

signal.description: The signal that ended it, such as `SIGKILL`.

stderr_tail.description: The last 64 KiB of its stderr, cut where a character starts.

product.description: The Product the engine runs as.

product_major.description: The major of its Product version, which names its per-major state.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the engine speaks.

EngineInstance.description: One engine process, new each time an engine starts: the positions of its events count within it. A Client compares it for equality only.

EnginePanickedDetails.description:
What `engine_panicked` details: what ended, never the panic's own text,
which stays in the crash report.

crash_report.description: The crash report's file name, when one was written.

id.description: The ID of what ended, when it has one, such as a Run's.

EngineStep.description: The engine's step that raised a Human pause.

oneOf.description: A login recovery (ADR 0006).
The Challenge ladder (ADR 0035).

EnqueueDocument.description: The document a handler read, against which its relative URLs resolve.

base_href.description: The `href` of its first `<base>` element, as written.

url.description: The URL the document was reached at, after every redirect.

Enqueued.description:
The Frontier's answer to a seed or an enqueue (ADRs 0079 and 0093): a
value, never an error, since a request is one among many.

oneOf.description: The Frontier admitted it as a crawl request.

id.description: The crawl request's ID within the Run.

url.description:
Its URL as the WHATWG URL Standard parsed it, resolved against
its base: the URL its handler receives.

oneOf.description: The Frontier did not admit it.

reason.description: Why.

url.description: Its URL as it was given.

EnqueuedBatch.description:
What `$/enqueued` carries: the answer of each seed of one `$/seeds`
batch, in the batch's order.

EnqueuedLink.description: What became of one element an `enqueueLinks` locator matched.

oneOf.description: The Frontier admitted its link as a crawl request.

id.description: The crawl request's ID within the Run.

url.description: Its URL as parsed and resolved, the URL its handler receives.

oneOf.description: The Frontier did not admit its link.

reason.description: Why.

oneOf.description: The element has no `href`.
The program's Payload function skipped it, returning `null`.

EnqueuedLinks.description:
What `crawl_request.enqueue_links` answers: what became of each element
its locator matched, in document order.

EquivalentForm.description:
Two spellings of one host's URLs a learned `equivalent_form` merges
(ADR 0120), each learned on evidence: a redirect from one to the
other, pairs of pages of matching signatures, or pages whose
`rel=canonical` differs from their URL only by it.

oneOf.description: One leading `www.` label against the bare host, the rule's host.
`http` against `https`.
A path with a trailing slash against the same path without it.
A final `index.html` against its folder.
A final `index.php` against its folder.

ErrorData.description:
What a failure's `data` holds: its Error code, whether the same call may
succeed when made again, and the code's own details.

code.description: The Error code, or the name of the protocol failure.

retryable.description: Whether the same call may succeed when made again.

ErrorGroup.description: The seven groups of Error codes, named for their remedy (ADR 0079).

oneOf.description: The program is wrong.
A policy, a Limit, a lock or a person refused.
The page or site never reached the state the call needed.
The Model provider's answer was unusable.
The deadline passed.
Something Goodfetch depends on is unreachable or gone.
A bug in Goodfetch.

code.description:
One of JSON-RPC's predefined codes for a protocol failure; otherwise
the numeric class of the Error code's group, from −32000 to −32099.

data.description: The Error code and its details.

message.description: What went wrong, for people; never matched on.

ErrorResponse.description: The reply to a call that failed.

id.description: The call's id, or `null` when the engine could not read one.

EvaluateParams.description:
What `page.evaluate` takes: the page, the function's source, its
argument and its world.

arg.description: Its one argument, JSON; absent for none.

function.description:
The page function's JavaScript source: a function, called with
`arg`, or an expression, which takes none.

world.description: Where it runs; the main world when absent.

Evaluated.description:
What `page.evaluate` answers: the function's result, awaited when it is
a promise.

value.description: The result as JSON; absent when it was `undefined`.

EventBatch.description:
What `$/events` carries: a batch of one subscription's events, in the
order of their positions.

id.description:
The id of the streaming call whose events it carries: a
subscription's `events.subscribe` call, or a `page.on` call, whose
page's events go only to it.

data.description: Its payload, of the type the catalog gives the event.

dropped.description:
For a telemetry event, how many of the same kind and scope it
replaced unsent.

event.description: The catalog's name of the event.

after.description:
The last event the Client read, `{engine_instance, position}`: the
subscription resumes after it, or starts with `events.resync` when
the engine no longer holds it or another engine instance gave it, as
after a Daemon restart. Absent, it starts with the next event.

system_info.description:
Whether it also takes `engine.system_info`, the Resource governor's
periodic readings; false by default, so a subscription that reads
only what changes sees no periodic event.

Evidence.description: What a test saw, beside its checks.

messages.description:
The scripted messages exchanged, for a Client conformance case (ADR
0069).

observations.description:
What the Proving ground observed on the server side, as it reported
it.

Executable.description:
The executable a Journey variant drove: its Product and the Product
version it reports (ADRs 0084 and 0090).

file.description: The path of the file Windows refused to start.

oneOf.description: A Product's executable, which can run its major's Daemon.

A program that links the engine through a Product's Rust crate: its
builds are kept, but it never runs the Daemon.

ExplainedSetting.description: One setting as `config explain` shows it.

applied.description:
Whether this engine applies it: `false` for a key only the other
Product honours, which a shared file may hold (ADR 0087).

cap.description: An Operator policy's cap on it, if any.

fixed_for_run.description:
Whether it is fixed for a Run's life: a resume that changes it is
refused with `setting_not_applicable`, and only a new Run takes
another value (ADRs 0102 and 0120).

key.description: Its key.

locked_by.description:
The layer that locked it, if any: an Operator policy's lock, a
Recipe that declares it without exposing it, or the default for an
honesty guarantee.

origin.description: For the run layer, where the value came from.

preset.description:
When a level's preset gave the value, at `layer`, that level, which
`config explain` shows as "preset of `run_state.durability: full`"
in place of the layer (ADR 0142).

products.description: The Products that honour it, from its Product mark (ADR 0095).

user_settable.description:
Whether user configuration may set it: its authority lets user
configuration hold it and no lower layer locked it, so a person
surface may offer its user-level value for editing (ADR 0031).

value.description:
The effective value, or for a key this engine does not apply, the
value its highest layer wrote.

weakens.description:
Whether its value weakens a guarantee class or switches off a costly
control, which the results it touches are marked with (ADR 0028).

yields_to.description:
The setting its value yields to, with that setting's value and
layer, when one that is set keeps its value from taking effect:
`fetch.http_from` away from `browser` yields to the Run's
`session.source`, whose Sessions hold a login and so send their HTTP
from the browser (#2418).

Export.description: What `run.export` answers once the Export's file is whole (ADR 0103).

last_number.description: The number of the last Record it holds, 0 when it holds none.

run_epoch.description:
The run epoch of the Run's state it was written from, which its ID
and its kept file's name carry too, so a destination that compares
and sets refuses the Export of a copy an older run epoch fenced
(ADR 0003).

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, in lowercase hexadecimal.

ExportCompression.description:
How an Export's bytes are compressed: the whole file, once written in
its format.

oneOf.description: Not compressed.
One gzip member (RFC 1952).
One Zstandard frame (RFC 8878).

ExportFormat.description: An Export's format, named, never inferred from a file name (ADR 0103).

oneOf.description:
One JSON array of the Records' values, indented as
`export.json.indent` says.
One Record's value per line, each line ended by a line feed.

RFC 4180 CSV: a header row of the fields seen, then one row per
Record, each line ended by CR LF.

One XLSX workbook of one sheet: a header row of the fields seen,
then one row per Record.

One HTML document holding one table: a header row of the fields
seen, then one row per Record.

One GitHub Flavored Markdown table: a header row of the fields seen,
then one row per Record.

One XML document: a root element named by `export.xml.root` holding
one element per Record named by `export.xml.record`, each field an
element of its name (`field` with a `name` attribute where its name
is no XML name), an object's fields as elements, an array's values
as `item` elements, and `null` an empty element with
`xsi:nil="true"`.

One Apache Parquet file of one column per field seen, typed: a
column whose values are all `true` or `false` is boolean, all whole
numbers a 64-bit integer, all numbers a 64-bit float, and any other
a string holding each cell's text, every column nullable.

One Apache Avro object container file of one record per Record,
with one field per field seen, typed as Parquet's columns are, each
field's name made a valid Avro name with the field's own in its
`doc`.

One Apache Arrow IPC file of one column per field seen, typed as
Parquet's columns are.

One RSS 2.0 feed named after the Dataset, of one item per Record,
its title, link, date and summary taken from the fields the
`export.feed.*` settings name.

One Atom feed named after the Dataset, of one entry per Record, its
title, link, date and summary taken from the fields the
`export.feed.*` settings name.

ExportId.description:
An Export of a Run, named by the engine when its file is whole:
`<run_id>.export-<run_epoch>-<sha256>`, the run epoch of the Run's
state it was written from (ADR 0003) and the SHA-256 of its bytes in
lowercase hexadecimal, so two Exports of the same bytes under one run
epoch are one file.

path.description:
The program's path, absolute, which an Attached engine writes
itself; any other engine leaves it to the SDK and sends the file's
bytes instead.

ExportSaved.description: What `export.save_as` answers once the file is whole.

run_epoch.description: The run epoch the Export was written under (ADR 0003).

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, in lowercase hexadecimal.

written.description:
Whether the engine wrote the program's path itself; when not, the
`$/chunk` notifications before this answer carried every byte, and
the SDK writes the path.

ExportStreamed.description: What `export.stream` answers once it sent every byte.

run_epoch.description: The run epoch the Export was written under (ADR 0003).

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, in lowercase hexadecimal.

ExportedAuditEntry.description:
One entry of an exported Audit log, one line of its JSONL: the entry
and the hash that chains it to the line before it.

chained.description:
Whether its hash chains it to the entry before it: `false` for an
entry of a Run whose `security.audit_chain` was off, whose hash is
`SHA-256` of 32 zero bytes and its own canonical JSON alone, and
which `audit verify` steps over while it verifies the chain around
it; left out when chained.

details.description:
What its kind records, such as a Secret reference and the domain it
was sent to, never a secret's value.

hash.description:
`SHA-256(previous hash ‖ RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the entry)`, in
lowercase hex; an anchor's is the last pruned entry's.

kind.description: Its kind, a value of the shared type `audit_kind`.

layer.description:
The settings layer its event came from, such as an Operator policy
that switched a control off; none where no layer applies.

run_id.description: The Run it happened in; none outside a Run.

sequence.description: Its place in the chain, from 1.

surface.description:
The surface the actor acted through, such as `kennel` for a person
in the Kennel; none for the engine's own events.

ExtractionFollow.description: Which pages a code-free crawl fetches beyond its seeds.

oneOf.description:
Every link of every page the crawl's scope admits: each `a[href]`
of the page, admitted as `enqueueLinks` admits it.

The entries of the sitemaps each seed's site names in its
robots.txt, read as a sitemap seed of that robots.txt reads them,
and no page's links.
The seeds alone.

requests.description: The latest outcome of each such request, in commit order.

FeatureId.description: A Feature's ID, `<kind>:<id>`, such as `row:CO-18` or `story:3-18`.

FetchTier.description:
A tier that fetches a crawl request's document (ADR 0020), from the
cheapest up.

oneOf.description:
An HTTP request, over reqwest in `standard` and `identified`
Sessions.
The site's own API, found from its pages.
A request sent from a browser page's context.
A browser that runs scripts without layout.
Collie's browser page.

FieldFilter.description: A condition on one top-level field of a Record.

oneOf.description: The field equals this JSON value.

The field is text holding this text, compared code point by code
point, case included.

FieldLocator.description:
What finds a field's element, named by `kind`: a CSS selector or an
`XPath` expression, each read alike on every tier, a page a fetch tier
serves from its document reading it as a browser reads it.

oneOf.description: A CSS selector.

An `XPath` 1.0 expression that finds nodes, with no namespace
prefix and no variable; a value field reads the first node it finds
in document order, when that node is an element, and a list every
element it finds. Under a row's element it is evaluated with that
element as its context node.

FieldMatch.description:
The `match` before a field's transform (ADR 0123): a capture group of a
regular expression, in the `regex` crate's syntax (ADR 0081), over the
text read; that group's text is what the transform reads.

group.description: The capture group, 1 by default; 0 is the whole match.

FieldTransform.description:
A field's Value transform (ADR 0123), named by `kind`, each
locale-dependent one stating its locale, a BCP 47 tag. A `number`,
`date` or `date_time` reads the machine-readable value of a `<time
datetime>`, a `<data value>` or an element's `content` attribute in its
invariant form (ISO 8601, a plain decimal with a dot), whatever the
locale; a text printed for people is read under its locale's CLDR
forms: a number in its digits, separators and grouping, a date or a
date and time in one of its short, medium or long forms with a
four-digit year; any other text is not a value.

oneOf.description: The text read: a string.

An integer or decimal: a JSON number, never through a float, so a
decimal a JSON number cannot hold exactly is not a value.
A date: `YYYY-MM-DD`.

A date and time: RFC 3339 with its offset, the one the text states,
else `time_zone`'s at that time; one stating neither is not a value.

time_zone.description: The time zone, an IANA name, of a text that states none.

os_code.description: The OS's own name for the error, such as `ENOSPC`, or none.

path.description:
On the engine's side, the folder where it keeps the Run; on the
program's, its path as given.

reason.description:
Why, as Rust's `io::ErrorKind` name in `snake_case`, such as
`storage_full` or `read_only_filesystem`, or `other`.

FilesUpgraded.description:
What `upgrade-files --json` prints (spec #608): the files of the new
major's copy, by their path in Goodfetch home; every list empty when
Goodfetch home holds no older major's files.

refused.description:
The files the new major already held otherwise, which it refused
to overwrite and kept.

unchanged.description:
The files the new major already held as the older major has them,
as after an earlier run.

upgraded.description: The files it gave the new major from the older major's.

FillParams.description:
What `locator.fill` takes: the locator whose field it fills, and the
text.

value.description: The text the field holds afterwards; an empty text clears it.

FindingId.description: A part of the installation `doctor` checks.

oneOf.description:
Goodfetch home: whether it can be written, and whether its Operator
policy and user configuration can be read.

The list of installed executables, in which this one records
itself (ADR 0098).
The Daemon of this executable's major: whether it runs and answers.
Whether the running Daemon is of this executable's version.

Whether the browser build a Run launches by default is in the
Browser cache.

FindingStatus.description: Whether a part of the installation is in order.

oneOf.description: It is.
It works, but something may fail or slow down later.
Something that needs it fails until the fix is applied.
The Run's setting.
The setting of the request's Label.

Form.description:
The form a Client's user writes names in (ADR 0099), which the engine
renders the names and targets of its messages in.

oneOf.description: The TypeScript SDK, and Code mode.
The Python SDK.
A Rust program.
The CLI.
The MCP server and the Framework adapters.

The catalog's own names: Integrations and the HTTP
listener.

fix.description: What to do: upgrade the engine, or run `upgrade-files`.

supported.description: The version this engine reads up to.

FormatsParams.description: What `page.formats` takes: the page, and the formats it asks for.

FormatsRequest.description:
The formats a `page.formats` call asks for, each `true` or its options:
one value, which a Record can carry and a Dataset's schema can be
generated from (ADR 0103). A format left out is left out of the result.

contacts.description:
The e-mail addresses, telephone numbers and social profiles the
page shows.

html.description: The page's HTML: its main content by default.

images.description: The page's images, each with its URL resolved and its `alt`.

links.description: The page's links, each with its URL resolved.

markdown.description: The page's content as Markdown, with GFM's tables.

media.description: The page's video and audio sources, each with its URL resolved.

metadata.description:
The page's metadata: its title, description, canonical URL,
language, Open Graph and Twitter tags, JSON-LD blocks and microdata
items.

tables.description: The page's tables, as rows of cells.

text.description: The text of the page's main content, a paragraph per block.

GotoParams.description:
What `page.goto` takes: the page, the URL it goes to, and when it
answers.

timeout.description:
How long the navigation may take, in milliseconds, at least 1:
absent for `timeout.navigation`, `null` for none, though an
enclosing timeout still applies (ADR 0080). Its waits for permits
count against it no more than against the setting.

wait_until.description: When the navigation answers; `load` when absent.

GovernorLevel.description: How loaded the engine is, as its governor judges it.

oneOf.description: Every reading has headroom: concurrency may rise.
A reading passed `governor.pressure`: concurrency drops.
Memory passed `governor.critical`, or the host's is critical.

GuaranteeClass.description:
What a Sink's probe proves of its destination (ADR 0026), from the
strongest.

oneOf.description: A stale run epoch is refused in the same transaction as the write.
A stale run epoch cannot overwrite a Record, but can add one.

A retry lands on the same key, sometimes only within a
deduplication window.

A Record may arrive more than once; the receiver deduplicates on its
delivery ID.

HandlerFailedDetails.description:
What `handler_failed` details: the exception the handler failed with
(ADR 0109).

exception_stack.description: The frames of the program's code, as one text; empty from Rust.

exception_type.description:
The exception's type name: `BoxError` or `panic` from Rust (ADR
0109).

HandlerSkip.description: A handler's skip of its request: `ctx.skip(message)` (ADR 0093).

HeaderCharacter.description: A character no header value may hold.

oneOf.description: A carriage return, U+000D.
A line feed, U+000A.
A NUL, U+0000.

character.description: The first character its value may not hold.

HealthProbe.description: Which of the ops listener's probes `daemon health` answers.

oneOf.description: `/livez`'s: whether the Daemon is live.
`/readyz`'s: whether it is ready to take a new Run.

domain.description:
The domain's key, its registrable domain unless `crawl.domain_keys`
names another.

next_admitted_at.description: When it is next admitted; none until a request in flight ends.

client_surface.description:
On a gateway's `hello` (surface `cloud`), the surface of the Client
whose Connection it relays, such as `mcp` for a model's: the engine
holds the Connection to that surface's rules, a model's settings
included (ADR 0092), and the gateway's mark only words
`not_in_product` (ADR 0095). None on the gateway's own Connection;
any other surface names none.

form.description:
The form its user writes names in (ADR 0099), which every SDK
declares; without one, the engine takes its surface's.

handlers.description:
The program's SDK handlers, their names by Plugin kind, as
`connect()` registers them (ADR 0104). The only handler of a kind
that one setting chooses becomes that setting's value at the
connection scope, with the origin `registered`, beneath every
other run-layer value. A kind the engine's Product lacks refuses
the `hello`.

keep_daemon_alive.description:
On a Kennel's `hello` (surface `kennel`), asks a Daemon to count the
Connection as a Client that keeps it alive, holding off its idle
stop and a handover to its major's pick as every other surface's
Connection does (ADR 0141). Read only from a `kennel` Connection,
and ignored on any other surface's.

log_level.description:
The level of the engine's log events the Client receives as `$/log`
notifications, until `connection.set_log_level` changes it; none,
as `off`, receives none (ADR 0078).

needs.description:
The Product the Client needs, which every surface but a Browser
host's must name (ADR 0095).

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the sender speaks.

settings.description:
The Connection's own settings, nested by key: the run layer at the
connection scope, which every Run it starts inherits beneath its
own (ADR 0083). A key the connection scope does not take is refused
with `setting_not_applicable`, and the `hello` with it.

token.description: The Daemon's token; an Attached engine needs none.

HelloResult.description: What an engine answers to a `hello` it accepts.

engine_instance.description:
The engine process, new each time an engine starts: the positions
of its events count within it, so a Client that meets a new one
resyncs (ADR 0031).

max_calls_in_flight.description:
How many calls the engine keeps in flight on this Connection: one
more is refused with `too_many_calls`, so a Client sends at most
this many at once and queues the rest in the order they were made
(ADR 0038; issue 2529). Absent from an engine that sets no cap, such
as the Scripted engine.

private_endpoint.description:
An Attached engine's private endpoint, reported to the Client of its
stdio alone: where that Client's `workers=N` handler processes, and a
Daemon forwarding a live action, connect (ADRs 0024 and 0031).

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the engine speaks.

timeouts.description:
Each `timeout.*` setting the engine's Product honours, as it
resolved at the Connection's layers (the engine's, beneath the
`hello`'s own `settings`), in milliseconds: a call the Client queues
past `max_calls_in_flight` with no timeout of its own fails at its
setting's value with `deadline_exceeded`, `waited_for`
`calls_in_flight` (ADR 0038's note of 2026-11-21; issue 3193). A
setting that resolves no timeout is left out; empty from an engine
that resolves none, such as the Scripted engine.

stage.description: The stage of the second Hook, the one refused.

HookFailedDetails.description:
What `hook_failed` details: the Hook, and the exception as
`handler_failed`'s details name a handler's (ADR 0079's notes of
2026-10-24 and 2026-10-27).

exception_stack.description: The frames of the program's code, as one text; empty from Rust.

exception_type.description:
The exception's type name: `BoxError` or `panic` from Rust (ADR
0109).

label.description:
The request's Label, or none at a lifecycle stage, which has no
request, and outside a crawl.

stage.description: The stage the Hook ran at.

wrapped_code.description:
The Goodfetch code raised inside the Hook, such as
`header_forbidden`, or none for the program's own exception.

hooks.description:
The Hooks in code its run file records, as its crawl declared them:
their names, stages and scopes, never their code.

closest.description:
The closest name the crawl's Hooks carry, or none when it has no
Hook.

HtmlFormat.description: The `html` format of a request: `true`, or its options.

HtmlKind.description: Which of the page's HTML an `html` format holds.

oneOf.description:
The document as served, or as the DOM stands on a browser tier,
before the Clean-up rules: what `content()` returns there.
The document after the Clean-up rules' cosmetic rules.
The main content the extractor finds, the default.

kind.description: Which of the page's HTML it holds.

HttpBody.description: The body a crawl request is sent with (ADR 0093): its bytes in Base64 (RFC 4648, with padding).

HttpListenerToken.description:
What `daemon http-listener-token --json` prints: the token the
Daemon's HTTP listener takes, the one credential a command prints, on
stdout alone (spec #608).

HttpMethod.description: The method a crawl request is sent with (ADR 0093): an RFC 9110 token, `GET` by default; `DELETE`, `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `POST` and `PUT` are uppercased as Fetch normalizes them, and `CONNECT`, `TRACE` and `TRACK` are refused.

HttpsUrl.description: An https:// URL with a host.

HumanPause.description: A Human pause waiting for a person (ADR 0092).

deadline.description:
When it ends unanswered: the first of `timeout.human_pause` and, in
a scheduled run, its pause timeout; none when it waits without
limit.

raised_by.description: Whether the program or the engine raised it.

reason.description: Why, as the program or the engine said it.

until.description: The condition that ends it by itself, as text.

Image.description: An image of the page: an ``, in document order.

alt.description:
Its `alt`: empty for an image marked decorative, `null` when it has
none.

src.description: Its `src` as the document writes it.

url.description:
Its `src` resolved against the document's base URL; `null` when it
does not parse.

InFlightPhase.description: Where a request in flight is.

oneOf.description: Its document is being fetched.
Its handler handles it.

Its handler waits for a navigation gate's permit: a navigation of
its page waits for its domain's Politeness, and its handler timeout
does not run meanwhile (ADR 0093).

InFlightRequest.description: A request being fetched or handled (ADR 0102).

tier.description: The fetch tier that fetches its document, when one does.

InitScriptEnded.description: What an init script's subscription answers when its page closes.

oneOf.description: It was downloaded and checked now.
It was already there, with its pinned digest.

InstalledBuild.description: One build `browser install` made sure of.

outcome.description: Whether it was downloaded now or already there.

InstalledExecutable.description: One executable that ran on this machine (ADR 0098).

copy.description:
Its versioned copy in the Browser cache, from which a Daemon runs
(ADR 0024), once one was made.

kind.description: What it is.

last_seen.description: When it last ran, in RFC 3339.

modified_at.description: When its file was last modified then, in RFC 3339.

path.description: Its absolute path when it last ran.

pins.description:
The browser builds and other cache downloads its version pins, its
versioned copy included once a Daemon runs from it.

product.description: The Product it is, or whose Rust crate it links.

size.description:
The size of its file in bytes then, which with `modified_at` tells
whether the file at `path` is still this executable.

InstalledExecutables.description:
The list of installed executables, `installed-executables.json` in
Goodfetch home (ADR 0098). Newer versions of the format only add, so an
engine keeps every entry and field it does not know when it rewrites the
list.

executables.description: One entry per executable, at one path and one Product version.

format_version.description: The version of this format the list was written in.

InstalledService.description:
The per-user service of one major that `daemon install` registered,
recorded in `daemon-service.json` in the major's per-major folder (ADRs
0024, 0031 and 0098): what starts the major's pick, from which versioned
copy, and the socket its service manager listens on for it.

executable.description:
The versioned copy in the Browser cache that the service starts,
which starts its major's pick.

files.description: The files that define it to the service manager.

manager.description: The service manager it is registered with.

name.description:
Its name there: a launch agent's label, a user unit's name without
its suffix, or a logon task's path.

socket.description:
The socket the service manager listens on and hands the Daemon it
starts at the first connection, or `None` where the OS has no socket
activation (Windows).

InstalledSkill.description: One skill `skill install` made sure of.

path.description: Its folder.

InternalDetails.description:
What `internal` details: the object whose table refused the event, its
state and the event, as the engine names them.

InvalidRecord.description:
One Record that does not hold for its Dataset, as `record_invalid`
names it.

issues.description: Each way it does not hold, at least one.

position.description:
Its position, from 0, among the Records pushed together, or among
those of the handler's answer.

oneOf.description: IPv4.
IPv6.

Journey.description:
One Journey: a goal a person reaches through its Product's public
surfaces, written as steps from a starting state to an outcome checked
from outside the engine (ADR 0063).

area.description: The number of the ADR 0037 area whose spec owns the Journey.

covers.description:
The Feature IDs the Journey exercises, each `<kind>:<id>`, such as
`row:CO-18` for a row of ADR 0037's matrix or `story:3-18` for a user
story.

goal.description:
What the person achieves and what MUST be true at the end, in RFC
2119 words, readable as a specification without the code. It never
changes under the Journey's ID.

id.description: `J-` and three to nine digits, equal to the file's name.

product.description:
The Product whose executable and SDK packages the Journey drives:
Collie when Collie carries every step, Foxhound otherwise (ADR 0094).

proving_ground.description:
The Proving ground data the Journey starts from; absent when its goal
touches no page.

reason.description: Why a retired Journey was retired.
