The engine's own resolver, which reads the system's resolver
configuration and hosts file and asks its name servers itself.
The operating system's resolver, on macOS and Windows.

Navigated.description:
What a navigation answers: the document's response, or none for a
navigation within the same document, to a URL no server answers, such as
`about:blank`, to a file the browser downloads instead of showing, which
`page.download` reports, or back or forward from the last entry of the
page's history. A 404 or a 500 is a response, a value.

error.description:
The browser's network error, such as `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`,
when the browser named one.

url.description:
The URL the navigation went to; none when the page's history, which
names it for a reload or a step back or forward, did not read.
The URL of the navigation that was superseded.

domain.description:
The registrable domain whose consent walls the next runs accept, as
a `consent_wall` item names it, or `*` for every domain.

NeedsYouChange.description: What `needs_you.changed` carries: one change of the list.

oneOf.description: An item appeared, or changed: it as it is now.
An item left the list.

reason.description: Why.
Why, such as the site's objection; required.

dismissed.description:
Whether it hid the item: false when the list no longer holds it, or
its source does not let a person dismiss it.

NeedsYouItem.description: One thing waiting for a person.

actions.description:
The catalog operations a person may answer it with, such as
`needs_you.dismiss`; empty when only something outside the engine,
such as freeing space, resolves it.

details.description:
Its kind's own fields, which the kind's value in the catalog names:
for `storage_level`, `level` and `folder`; for
`run_stopped_by_storage`, `folder`; for `run_stopped_by_limit`,
`limit`, `amount`, `needs` and, for a Recipe's Run, `recipe`; for
`consent_wall`, `domain`; for `wall_refetch_stopped`, `domain`,
`cause`, the `layer` and `file` that list it and `only_star`; for
`certificate_changed`, `host`, `person`, `pinned_spki_sha256` and
`presented_spki_sha256`.

id.description:
Its ID, which names this one occurrence for good: a Run stopped
again by storage after a resume is another item.

kind.description:
What it is, a value of a type both Products share, such as
`storage_level`; a Client shows a kind it does not know by its
summary.

run.description: The Run it is about, if any.

schedule.description: The Schedule it is about, if any.

summary.description:
What waits, in the engine's English, which a Client shows for a kind
it has no words of its own for.

NeedsYouList.description:
What `needs_you.list` answers: one page of the items, the longest
waiting first.

items.description: The items, by `since`, then by ID.

next.description:
Where the next page starts, as the next call's `after`; absent on
the last page.

after.description: The `next` of the page read before: the list goes on after it.

kinds.description: Only the items of these kinds; every kind when absent.

NeedsYouRemoval.description: Why an item left the list.

oneOf.description:
What waited is resolved: by a person, here or elsewhere, or by its
Run.
A person dismissed it.

domain.description: The registrable domain, as a `wall_refetch_stopped` item names it.

instead_of_star.description:
When only `*` covers the domain in its layer, the registrable
domains that replace `*` there, the domain itself not among them.

NewPageParams.description:
What `run.new_page` takes: the Run whose default Session opens the page,
and the page's own settings.

settings.description:
The page's own settings, nested by key (ADR 0083), which it takes
over its Session's and its Run's: `content.extractor`, the
main-content step its formats read with. Any other key is refused
with `setting_not_applicable`, as only its Session or its Run sets
it.

NewSessionPageParams.description:
What `session.new_page` takes: the Session, and the page's own
settings.

settings.description:
The page's own settings, nested by key (ADR 0083), which it takes
over its Session's and its Run's: `content.extractor`, the
main-content step its formats read with. Any other key is refused
with `setting_not_applicable`, as only its Session or its Run sets
it; the Session's Access mode, Identity profile and proxy only its
opening sets.

NewSessionParams.description:
What `run.new_session` takes: the Run whose Session it opens, the
Session's own source and its own settings.

settings.description:
The Session's own settings, nested by key: `filter_lists.ads`,
`.trackers`, `.annoyances`, `.first_party_scripts`,
`browser.block_resources` and `live_view.hiding` choose its pages'
Clean-up rules over the Run's, and `browser.service_workers` whether
a site's service workers run in them, and `session.page_check` the
Page check its pages are judged against, and `content.extractor`
the main-content step their formats read with; `browser.access_mode`
and the `stealth.*` items its Access mode and Identity profile, and
the `proxy.*` keys its proxy, which it keeps for its life.
`session.source` is refused here with `setting_not_applicable`,
as the call's own `source` sets it, and so is any other key, which
only the Run sets.

source.description:
`session.source` for this Session alone: left out, the Run's or the
connection's applies; `null`, the Session opens fresh (ADRs 0083
and 0092).

NotAddedAtCommit.description:
A request an attempt's enqueue, `enqueueLinks` call or seed answered
`added`, with its ID, that the attempt's commit did not add (ADR 0093):
the commit admits each staged request again on the run file as it then
stands, and another attempt's commit may have added the request
meanwhile, or a rule learned since refuses it. Its ID names no crawl
request.

duplicate_of.description:
The crawl request it is a duplicate of, when another request was
admitted under its identity first.

reason.description: Why the commit did not add it.

NotAddedReason.description: Why the Frontier did not add a request (ADRs 0093 and 0120).

oneOf.description:
The Frontier already admitted a request of the same identity: its
method, its URL's key and its body's hash, or its declared `key`.

Its URL is outside the crawl's scope (`crawl.scope.*`); or, for a
nested sitemap, it is on a host its sitemap seed does not read
sitemaps on.
The Run's domain policy refuses its host.
It is deeper than `crawl.max_depth`.
The crawl already admitted `crawl.max_requests` requests.

Its URL's scheme is one the crawl cannot fetch: only `http` and
`https` are.

The WHATWG URL Standard's parser refuses its URL, or it is relative
where nothing gives it a base, as a seed is.
Its URL is longer than `crawl.max_url_length`.
Its URL's path has more segments than `crawl.max_path_segments`.

A segment of its URL's path repeats more than
`crawl.max_segment_repeats`.

A sitemap nested more levels under its sitemap seed than
`crawl.max_sitemap_nesting` (ADR 0093).

The first entry of `crawl.path_budgets` whose pattern its URL's path
and query match already counted that entry's `max_requests`.

Its URL's path falls under a trap the Frontier learned and closed
(ADR 0005): a path pattern whose pages brought no new page and no
URL outside it, which leaves a finished Run `unverified`.
A sitemap entry no rule of its sitemap seed matches (ADR 0093).

On the browser tier, its link is one a person cannot see, a
`nofollow` one among them: a trap a crawl never enters (ADR 0035).

The `enqueueLinks` call that matched it already added its `limit`
links (ADR 0093).

NotCleaned.description: Why the clean-up did not run.

oneOf.description:
The engine cannot write the cache, such as a read-only
`GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` (ADR 0098).

fix.description: What to do instead.

handover.description:
Whether the refusing engine is a Daemon handing over to its major's
pick, which a Client of the major waits for and connects to (ADR
0098).

install.description:
The command that installs the Product `needs` from the engine's own
channel, which `fix` names; none behind Goodfetch Cloud's gateway,
where an install would not help (ADR 0096).

needs.description: The Product that carries what was asked.

requested.description: What was asked, such as an operation's name; `None` for a `hello`.

NotUnderstoodLimit.description:
A Limit flagged *must understand* that a Run's engine cannot evaluate,
as the Run stopped for it names it (ADR 0041): its scope, Usage kind,
currency and period as the ledger holds them.

currency.description: The currency it caps a price in, for a price Limit.

period.description: Its period; none for a Limit that never starts again.

reasons.description:
Why it is not `verified`: failed, missing or switched-off checks, an
early end, uncertain Effects.

reported.description: The model's claim, when it made one.

verdict.description:
The work's Verdict, which is not `verified`; one this reader does not
know is kept as received.

NothingCommitted.description: Why a succeeded request committed no Record (ADR 0103).

oneOf.description: Its handler pushed none.

Every Record it pushed was dropped or rejected, as its `records`
count.
`dataset.records` is off, so the crawl keeps no Record (ADR 0138).

NothingDone.description: Why a call that ends a Run did nothing (ADR 0102's G1).

oneOf.description: The start found the Run ended.

No seed reached a handler: each was refused when added or ended
before its handler ran, counted by why.

seeds.description:
How many seeds each reason kept from a handler: the reason an
enqueue answered, or how the request ended, by its skip reason,
Error code or Block cause, in the order of the reasons.

oneOf.description: A resume or a retry found nothing left.

Notification.description: A message that expects no reply, such as `$/cancel`.

Now.description: The word `now`: from the next commit on.

oneOf.description: From the next commit on.

OperatorPolicyRead.description: The Operator policy as `config.policy_read` reads it.

digest.description:
The digest of the file as read, which `config.policy_write` takes
back. It is the policy version a Run report names, `sha256:` and 16
hex digits, of the file's text, or of no text when there is none.

entries.description:
Every entry of its three tables, by table, then key, the other
Product's keys included.

found.description: Whether the file exists; a policy that does not sets nothing.

path.description: Its file's path.

OracleAnswer.description:
An oracle's answer for one Proving ground task: the task, the outcome,
and the rest of the Proving ground's answer as it came (what is missing,
extra or wrong, the tool's status, the oracle's time).

OracleOutcome.description:
The outcome the Proving ground's oracle gives a submitted result, whatever
status the tool reported (ADR 0025).

oneOf.description: Correct and complete.
Correct but missing Records, without claiming success.
Claimed success with wrong or missing data.
Neither correct nor a claimed success.
Every declared case ran and passed.
No case failed, but not every one ran, or none is declared.
A case failed.
Its handler returned, and what it staged was committed.
Its last attempt failed, and no retry is left.
A decision ended it: a skip is never retried.
The site refused it, with a Block cause.

OutcomeRequest.description: The crawl request an outcome ends.

depth.description: How many links away from a seed it is: 0 for a seed.

anyOf.description: After the outcome at this position, which a reader last read.

OutcomesAfter.description: Where `run.outcomes` starts: after a position, or from the next commit.

OverloadedBound.description:
A Connection's own bound on what it holds, as `connection_overloaded`
names it.

oneOf.description:
`connection.max_pending_calls`: the calls waiting for their answer,
sent or queued.

`connection.max_queued_write_bytes`: the bytes waiting to be written
to the engine.

PageBodyParams.description: What `page.body` takes: the body to read.

run_id.description: The Run whose folder holds it.

PageBodyRead.description: What `page.body` answers once it sent the last chunk.

noindex.description:
Whether the document is marked `noindex`, by a `noindex` or `none`
directive in its `X-Robots-Tag` header or a robots `meta` element:
a crawl takes such a page for a decoy (ADR 0035).

url.description: The URL of the document the navigation reached.

PageCloseParams.description:
What `page.close` takes: the page, and whether its `beforeunload`
handlers run.

run_before_unload.description:
Runs the page's `beforeunload` handlers first, whose dialog goes to
the page's dialog handlers; false when absent.

browser_exit.description:
How the browser process ended, when it is what was lost; none for a
renderer's crash alone.

PageDownload.description:
What `page.download` reports: a navigation of a page that the browser
turned into a download.

page_id.description: The page whose navigation it was.

suggested_filename.description: The file name the browser suggests for it.

PageEventName.description:
A page's event a program listens to, by its words (ADR 0099): each
SDK joins them as Playwright spells the event, such as `pageerror`.

oneOf.description: `page.console`.
`page.page_error`.
`page.request`.
`page.request_finished`.
`page.request_failed`.
`page.response`.
`page.web_socket`, with each socket's `web_socket.*` events.
`page.load`.
`page.dom_content_loaded`.
`page.crash`.
`page.close`.
`page.popup`.

PageExchange.description:
What `page.response` reports, and `page.wait_for_request_finished`
answers: a request and the response it got.

anyOf.description: The first element its locator finds.
Fields read under each element a base locator finds.

PageField.description: One named field (ADR 0147): a value field, a list or rows.

PageFired.description:
What `page.load`, `page.dom_content_loaded`, `page.crash` and
`page.close` report: the page whose main frame's document fired the
event, or that crashed or closed.

PageFormats.description:
What `page.formats` answers: the formats the request asked for, and
none it did not, with the document's URL, its base URL and, when a
format it asked for is read from the main content, whether the document
has main content. Text is as the document holds it, never repaired.

base_url.description:
The URL its relative URLs resolve against: its first `<base href>`,
else its URL.

contacts.description: Its contacts, when the request asked for them.

html.description: Its HTML of the kind the request named, when it asked for it.

images.description: Its images, when the request asked for them.

links.description: Its links, when the request asked for them.

main_content.description:
Whether it has main content, when the request asked for a format
read from it ([`FormatsRequest::reads_main_content`]).

markdown.description: Its content as Markdown, when the request asked for it.

media.description: Its media sources, when the request asked for them.

metadata.description: Its metadata, when the request asked for it.

tables.description: Its tables, when the request asked for them.

text.description: Its main content's text, when the request asked for it.

fix.description:
What to do instead, when the engine knows: a `ReferenceError`'s
fix names the argument, which is all a page function sees of the
program.

message.description: What the page said, or why the engine refused the function.

name.description:
The thrown error's name, such as `ReferenceError`; absent for a
thrown value that is no error, and for an expression given an
argument.

stack.description: The page's stack, when it gave one.

PageHandler.description: The handlers a program gives a page, which `page_handler_failed` names.

oneOf.description: A route's handler.
A dialog handler.

url.description:
The URL of the request it was answering, or of the document whose
dialog it was answering.

PageId.description: A page of a Run, named by the engine when it opens it.

memory.description:
What it held when measured, in bytes: its JavaScript heap and the
buffers it held.

PageOnDialogParams.description:
What `page.on_dialog` takes: the page whose dialogs its handler
answers.

PageOnEnded.description: What `page.on` answers when its page goes, closed or with its Run.

PageOnParams.description: What `page.on` takes: the page and the event listened to.

PageOpened.description:
What `run.new_page` and `session.new_page` answer: the page, and the
Session it belongs to, which `page.session()` returns.

session_id.description: Its Session: the Run's default Session for `run.new_page`.

PagePopup.description:
What `page.popup` reports: the page that opened a popup, and the
popup, a page of the same Session.

PageRead.description:
What `page.read` answers: each field's value by its name, and each
value the page did not give, with why.

unread.description:
Each null the page did not give, in the order read; absent where
every value was read.

values.description:
Each field's value, by name: a value field's value or null, a
list's array of values or nulls, rows' array of objects, each
holding every field of its row, null where its row lacks it. Its
names and types follow `fields` (`typed_by`), from which each SDK
types it (ADR 0147).

PageReadParams.description: What `page.read` takes: the page and its named fields.

PageRequest.description:
A request of a page, ADR 0085's `Request`: one per hop of a redirect
chain, each hop under its own `request_id`, as Playwright's
`redirectedFrom()` and `redirectedTo()` tell them apart.

failure.description: Why it failed, for `page.request_failed`; none otherwise.

headers.description:
Its headers as the browser sent them, their names in lowercase, as
Playwright gives them.

is_navigation_request.description:
Whether it loads the document of one of the page's frames, its main
frame's or an iframe's, as Playwright's `isNavigationRequest()`.

post_data.description: Its body, in Base64 (RFC 4648, with padding), when it has one.

redirect_chain.description:
The URLs of the hops a redirect led from before it, the first first;
empty when no redirect led to it.

redirected_from.description:
The `request_id` of the hop whose redirect led to it, Playwright's
`redirectedFrom()`; none at a request's first hop.

request_id.description:
The engine's ID for this hop, which `response.body` takes: the
browser's ID for the request at its first hop, and that ID with
`#` and the hop's number after each redirect.

resource_type.description:
What it loads, as Playwright's `resourceType()` names it: the
browser's name in lowercase, such as `document`, `fetch` or `xhr`.

PageRequestParams.description:
What `page.request` takes: the page whose Session sends the request, and
the request.

headers.description:
Headers set over those the browser sends, each name matched without
regard to case.

max_redirects.description:
How many redirects it follows, from 0, which answers the 3xx itself,
to 19, the default; past its count it raises `too_many_redirects`,
and a count above 19 is refused with `setting_invalid`.

PageResponse.description: The response to a request of a page, such as a navigation's document.

encoding.description:
For a navigation's document, the encoding the browser decoded it
with, as `document.characterSet` names it, such as `Shift_JIS` (ADR
0119); none for another response, and for a navigation that answered
at `commit`, before its document was decoded.

from_service_worker.description:
Whether a site's service worker supplied it, from its own cache or
through its own fetch (ADR 0121).

headers.description: Its headers, their names lower-cased, as the browser received them.

request_id.description:
The engine's ID for its request's hop, which `response.body` takes:
its request's `request_id`.

PageRouteParams.description:
What `page.route` takes: the page, and the URLs whose requests its
handler answers.

PageValueDirection.description: Which way a value outside JSON was going.

oneOf.description: The page function's result, checked in the page.
Its argument, refused before it is sent.

constructor.description: Its constructor's name, when it has one, such as `HTMLDivElement`.

direction.description: Whether the value was the result or the argument.

fix.description: What to do instead.

kind.description: Its kind.

path.description:
Where the first value outside JSON is, from `$`, the whole value,
such as `$.rows[2].cell`.

PageValueKind.description: The kind of a value outside JSON (ADR 0085).

oneOf.description: A DOM node, such as an element or a document.
A window, such as `window` itself.
`NaN`.
`Infinity` or `-Infinity`.
A `BigInt`.
A `Symbol`.
A function.
An object reached again inside itself.
A `Map`.
A `Set`.
A `Date`.
A `RegExp`.
An `Error`.

Any other object whose prototype is not `Object`'s, such as a
class's instance, a typed array or a promise inside a result.

PageWebSocket.description:
What `page.web_socket` reports: a WebSocket the page opened, whose
frames and close follow as `web_socket.*` events.

web_socket_id.description: The browser's ID for the socket, which its events name.

PanicEnded.description: What a panic in the engine ended (ADR 0148).

oneOf.description: One call; its Connection goes on.
One attempt of a crawl.
A Page.
A Session, with its Pages.
A browser, treated as crashed.
A Run, which ends `failed`.
A Connection, which ends as when its Client goes away.
The engine, which stops.

PathHazard.description: What makes a name or path unsafe.

oneOf.description: A `..` part, which climbs out of the folder.
A path from the root.
A Windows drive, absolute or drive-relative.
A Windows verbatim path, `\\?\`.
A Windows device path, `\\.\`.
A Windows UNC path.
A name Windows reserves for a device, with or without an extension.
A trailing dot or space, which Windows removes.
An NTFS alternate data stream, after a colon.
A character Windows forbids in a name: `<`, `>`, `"`, `|`, `?` or `*`.
A control character or a NUL.

A name not in Unicode's composed form (NFC), which APFS opens as the
composed name it equals.
A part longer than the 255 bytes a file system's name holds.
An empty part, or a `.` part.
A folder separator where one name alone is taken.

fix.description: What to change in the path argument.

os_code.description: The OS's own name for the error, such as `EACCES`, or none.

path.description: The program's path, as given.

reason.description:
Why, as Rust's `io::ErrorKind` name in `snake_case`, such as
`permission_denied` or `is_a_directory`.

name.description: The name or path, as given.

PatternConstruct.description: A construct of a URL pattern the engine's matcher cannot read (ADR 0081).

oneOf.description: A regular expression's look-ahead or look-behind, such as `(?=x)`.
A regular expression's back-reference, such as `\1`.

A glob's `{` inside another `{…}` group, which Playwright refuses
too.

A glob's `{` with no `}`, or `}` with no `{`, which Playwright
refuses too.

Any other construct outside the `regex` crate's syntax, or a
regular expression too large to compile; the message names it.

construct.description: The construct the engine cannot read.

fix.description: What to do instead.

pattern.description: The pattern as the call passed it.

oneOf.description: The program, with `page.pause()`.
The engine, at a step of its own.

issues.description:
Each way it does not fit the Label's JSON Schema; none when it is
too long.

label.description: The Label the Payload was enqueued under.

limit.description: The setting it is longer than, `crawl.payload.max_size`.

max_size.description: The setting's value, when it is too long.

size.description: Its JSON's length in bytes, when it is too long.

PayloadIssue.description: One way a Payload does not fit its Label's JSON Schema.

path.description: Where in the Payload, a JSON Pointer: empty for the Payload itself.

failing.description: How many of its pending requests' Payloads fail the new schema.

issues.description: How its Payload fails the new schema.

label.description: The Label whose Payload schema changed.

pending.description: How many of its requests are pending.

PaymentMark.description:
The payment of a Paid fetch, as a Record's Provenance marks it (ADR
0045).

amount.description: The amount charged, an exact decimal.

scheme.description: The payment scheme the site asked through.

Period.description:
The period a Limit counts over, in an explicit IANA time zone, so that
it never depends on the host's (ADR 0041).

time_zone.description: The IANA time zone its midnights are in, such as `Europe/Paris`.

PeriodLength.description: How long a period Limit counts before it starts again (ADR 0041).

oneOf.description: From one midnight to the next.
From Monday's midnight to the next Monday's.
From the first day's midnight to the next month's.

PermitRow.description:
One Permit in the per-user Politeness file (ADR 0053): a request in
flight under one key, such as a domain key, with the Run and run epoch
that hold it, so an engine reclaims the Permits of a Run whose writer
lock is free or held at a later epoch.

engine.description: The engine that took it, which gives it back itself.

epoch.description: The run epoch it was taken under (ADR 0003).

key.description: The key it counts under, such as a domain key.

run_folder.description: The Run's folder, whose writer lock tells whether the Run is live.

taken_at.description: When it was taken, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

Phone.description: A telephone number the page shows.

e164.description:
The number in E.164, such as `+33123456789`, when it carries its
country code or the document's language tag carries a region, and
it is a valid number there; `null` otherwise, as no country is
guessed.

text.description:
The text it was read from: its `tel:` link's text, else the number
as the text writes it.

value.description: The number as written: its `tel:` link's number, else the text's.

PinnedTask.description: A Proving ground task a Journey names.

digest.description: The digest the task list gives the task, which ignores the port.

id.description: The task's ID in the task list of the Journey's seed.

Pinner.description:
What pins an artifact, as an error's details name it, by its `kind`: a
Product version, or an installed Plugin that uses a Plugin runtime (ADRs
0098 and 0115).

oneOf.description: A Product version.
An installed Plugin, for the Plugin runtime it uses.

PlanReport.description: What a Run did with its Plan file (ADR 0091).

file.description: The Plan file's path, or none.

status.description: What became of its new versions.

steps_changed.description: The steps that changed, each Agent task one entry (ADR 0100).

PlanStatus.description: What became of a Run's new Plan versions (ADR 0091).

oneOf.description: Nothing changed.
They were written to the Plan file.
They wait for a person.
The Plan file is frozen.

Platform.description: The operating system and architecture a document's tests ran on.

arch.description:
The architecture, as Rust's `std::env::consts::ARCH` names it
(`x86_64`, `aarch64`).

os.description:
The operating system, as Rust's `std::env::consts::OS` names it
(`linux`, `macos`, `windows`).

PluginRun.description: A Plugin that ran in a Run (ADRs 0016 and 0033).

confinement_missing.description:
The parts of its confinement the host could not give, under a
reduced confinement the Operator policy allowed.

network_level.description: The network level it ran at.

PointInTime.description: A point in time in UTC, as RFC 3339.

key.description: The key it changes.

value.description: The key's new value; `null` removes it from the table.

digest.description: The digest the write was made against.

fix.description: What to do instead.

PolicyEntry.description:
One entry of the Operator policy: a key of one of its tables, and its
value.

key.description: Its key.

PolicyTable.description:
A table of the Operator policy: what it sets, what it sets and locks, and
its caps.

oneOf.description: `[settings]`: values it sets, which a higher layer may change.
`[lock]`: values it sets and locks.
`[cap]`: the most a count or a duration may be.

changes.description: The changes, made in order, in one write.

digest.description:

diff.description:

digest.description: The file's digest after the write, the version new Runs name.

Position.description: An event's position among every event of one engine, which only goes up; for a `page.on` call's own events, among that call's, from 1.

Presence.description:
Whether the state a Run index row points at is there (ADRs 0031 and

oneOf.description: Its state is at its location.

PressParams.description:
What `locator.press` takes: the locator whose element gets the key, and

key.description:
A key or a combination, such as `Enter`, `a` or `Shift+Tab`, by

PressureSource.description: The reading that holds the engine above `normal`.

oneOf.description: The engine and its children's memory, against the Memory allowance.
The host's own memory pressure, which counts as the engine's.

The Tokio workers' busy time.

PrivateEndpoint.description:
An Attached engine's private endpoint (ADRs 0024 and 0031): where it

Product.description:
One of Goodfetch's two Products (ADR 0084), by its mark as the catalog

oneOf.description: Browser automation; Foxhound contains it.
Crawling, which contains Collie.

helm_chart.description: Its Helm chart, an OCI artifact.

pypi.description: Its Python wheels on the Python Package Index.

client_protocol_version.description: The protocol version the Client's `hello` named.

engine_protocol_version.description: The protocol version the engine speaks.

handover.description:

The Proving ground a document's tests ran against: its version, which

username.description: The username the Session gave, if it gave one.

provider.description: The Proxy provider, as `proxy.provider` names it.

url.description: The URL the request went to.

error.description: The local error that kept the relay from opening.

A proxy tier of ADR 0021's ladder, from the cheapest up: a Session

oneOf.description: No proxy: the machine's own address.
A datacenter proxy.
An ISP proxy.
A residential proxy.
A mobile proxy, the top of the ladder.

error.description:
The browser's network error, such as
`net::ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED`, or the proxy's own error its

url.description:
The URL the request went to; none when the proxy failed the
Session's open, before any request.

PublicSigningKey.description:
A key directory's entry of one key: its public JSON Web Key, named by

kid.description: The key's ID, its RFC 7638 thumbprint, which each signature names.

x.description: The public key, in unpadded Base64url.

PushedRecord.description: One Record a handler pushed into a Dataset (ADR 0103).

QueryColumn.description: One column of a query's result.

type.description: Its SQL type, as DuckDB names it, such as `BIGINT` or `VARCHAR`.

reason.description: Why the statement was refused.

limit.description: `dataset.query.memory_limit`, its value in bytes and its layer.

oneOf.description: It does not parse.
It names a table, column, function or type that does not exist.
It is not one `SELECT` or `WITH` statement.
It names a run the query did not select.
It reads a file or URL.

Reached.description:
What `page.wait_for_url`, `page.wait_for_load_state` and
`locator.wait_for` answer once the state they waited for came.

ReachedLimit.description:
The Limit a Run cannot take more of: what `limit_reached` details, and

currency.description: The currency it caps a price in, for a price Limit.

period.description: Its period; none for a Limit that never starts again.

resets_at.description: When its period starts again; none for a Limit without one.

detached.description:
Whether the Run outlives the program (ADR 0102): closing its value
then frees only the value, `run.finish` waits for its end and
`run.stop` stops it.

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

recipe.description:
The Recipe: an installed Recipe's name, or the path to its
manifest.

recording.description: The Response recording the Run replays or records (ADR 0105).

settings.description: The Run's settings, nested by key: the run layer (ADR 0083).

timeout.description:
How long the Run may last, in milliseconds, at least 1, as
`timeout.run` for this Run: absent for the setting's value, `null`
for none.

RecordFilter.description: Which Records a page takes: those that meet every condition.

fields.description: Conditions on the Records' fields, every one met.

wall.description: The Wall marker a Record carries or not; absent takes both.

records.description: Each Record that does not hold, in position order, at least one.

RecordIssue.description: One way a Record does not hold for its Dataset.

path.description: Where in the Record, a JSON Pointer: empty for the Record itself.

RecordProvenance.description: How one committed Record was obtained.

certificate_exception.description:
The exception of `tls.accept_invalid_certs` its document's host was
reached through; none where its certificate verified.

clean_up_rules.description:
The digest, `sha256:<hex>`, of the Clean-up rules the Run holds to,
whose Run trace names their date and the release that applied them.

encoding.description:
The encoding the document was read in, and where it came from;
none for a request with no document.

origin.description:
The Response cache or Response recording that answered in place of
the network; none when the network did.

payment.description:
The payment of a Paid fetch of its page; none where nothing was
paid.

request_id.description: The ID of the crawl request whose attempt produced it.

robots_txt.description:
`ignored` when its page was fetched while
`site_preferences.respect_robots_txt` was off and
`site_preferences.mark_robots_txt_ignored` on, from a URL its
origin's robots.txt disallows, so a result taken against a site's
stated preferences can be found and removed; none otherwise.

tier.description:
The tier that fetched that request's document, and how it was
chosen; none where no document was fetched.

unread_fields.description:
Each field of a code-free crawl the page did not give, null in the
Record, with why; absent where every field was read.

value_transforms.description:
Each field whose value an engine Value transform gave, in the
order read; empty where the program parsed its own values.

wall.description: The Wall its page was read past; none where no Wall was met.

RecordRead.description: What `$/record` carries: the next Record a `run.records` call reads.

RecordSort.description:
The order of a page's Records: by one top-level field, Records that
lack it last, then by number.

Recording.description:
A Response recording a start names (ADR 0105): an input of the Run,
never a setting.

mode.description: Whether the Run replays the file or records it.

path.description:
The WARC 1.1 file, on the program's machine, relative to its working
directory.

RecordingMode.description: What a Run does with the Response recording its start names (ADR 0105).

oneOf.description:
Every request the Run would send to a site is answered from the
file, and one it lacks is refused, never sent.

The Run fetches as usual and, when it ends, replaces the file with
every response it received.

RecordingReport.description: What a Run did with the Response recording its start named (ADR 0105).

recorded_from.description: When the oldest of them was fetched.

recorded_to.description: When the newest of them was fetched.

responses_used.description: How many recorded responses it used.

RecordsRead.description:
What `run.records` answers once it sent the last Record: how many it
sent, and the number of the last, which a later call's `after` takes.

last.description:
The number of the last Record it sent, else the `after` it took, 0
without one.

RedirectLimit.description:
The count of redirects a fetch follows at most, and what set it (ADR
0118).

oneOf.description:
The browser's own count, 20 requests in a navigation's chain, its
first included, which a navigation cannot change: it follows 19
redirects (ADR 0118).

count.description:
The requests the chain may hold, its first included: 20, one
more than the redirects followed, which `hops` lists.

oneOf.description: A setting, such as `fetch.redirect.max`, at its resolved value.

count.description: The redirects it allows, the chain's first request left out.

oneOf.description:
A call's option, such as `page.request`'s `max_redirects`, by its
canonical name (ADR 0099).

count.description: The redirects it allows, the chain's first request left out.

domains.description: That layer's `wall.refetch_domains` now.

layer.description:
The layer that listed it, and now does not; none when no layer was
changed.

removed.description:
Whether its layer changed: false when neither user configuration
nor the Operator policy lists it, which then changed nothing and
recorded nothing.

Refused.description:
What a `value_invalid` refused: the key itself, or the value given for
it.

oneOf.description: The key.
The value.

RejectedRecord.description: One entry of a Dataset's rejection table.

data.description:
The Record as JSON, as it was pushed, never parsed by the schema it
failed.

hook.description: The Hook that rejected it; absent when the engine's own check did.

issues.description:
Each issue the check found, by its path, a JSON Pointer into the
Record; empty when a Hook rejected it with none.

number.description:
Its place in the Dataset's rejection table, from 1, in commit
order with no gaps, which `run.rejected_records`'s `after` takes.

reason.description: Why it was rejected.

request_id.description: The ID of the crawl request whose attempt pushed it.

ended.description:
Whether the table is read to its end: the Run has ended, or has no
live writer, and no entry follows `next`.

next.description: The number the next page starts after.

records.description: The entries after `after`, in number order.

collie_client.description: The Collie client packages both Products' SDKs build on (ADR 0095).

formats.description:
The version of every registered format the release shipped, read from
its tag's format registry.

plugins.description: The first-party Plugins, one OCI artifact per target (ADR 0094).

version.description: The Product version both Products carry (ADR 0090).

release.description:
One entry per stable release or patch; release candidates and
nightlies have none.

RemovedBuild.description: One build `browser clean` deleted, or would delete.

bytes.description: The bytes its files take on disk.

Reported.description:
The model's claim and its message, absent from a result when no model
claimed anything: the work stopped before a claim, or was replayed whole
(ADR 0100).

message.description: What it said with the claim, when it said something.

ReportedHookStage.description:
The stage a Hook that raised ran at, as `hook_failed` reports it, by
the catalog's name (ADR 0104): a crawl's Hooks in code run at the stages
whose answer changes the work, and Plugins and Script Hooks also at the
observe-only `request_ended`. A Run's lifecycle stage reads as a stage
this reader does not know, its name kept.

oneOf.description: Before each fetch of a request, its retries included.
After the request's final response, redirects followed.

Before a navigation to the request's URL, on the tiers that
navigate.
After that navigation.
Just before the handler, with its page, on every tier.
Before each Record the attempt staged commits.
Once a crawl request ended, with its outcome; observe-only.

by_error_code.description: The failed ones, by Error code.

The Error code the engine failed it with, with its details, when the
engine did, such as `egress_refused`.

error_text.description:
The browser's network error, such as `net::ERR_FAILED` for a request

blocked.

RequestId.description: A request's id, which its reply carries back.

RequestMeta.description:
What a request's `_meta` holds (ADR 0132), which its runtime writes and
never a program: its Trace context, with no Baggage, and the raw mark of
a call a program made through the raw `call` (ADR 0099). A closed
object: the engine refuses any other key. The schema checks only that
each Trace context field is a string: a receiver drops a value it cannot
use, and never fails the call for it.

raw.description:
Whether the program sent the call through the raw `call`, the way
down to an operation its SDK does not generate (ADR 0099): an SDK
sets it on that call alone, and refuses a `_meta` the program writes
into its params, so a program neither forges nor removes it. The
engine validates and enforces a raw call as any other.

traceparent.description:
The caller's span, as W3C Trace Context's `traceparent` header
holds it.

tracestate.description:
Its vendors' values, as W3C Trace Context's `tracestate` header
holds them.

by_block_cause.description: The blocked ones, by Block cause.

by_error_code.description: The failed ones, by Error code.

by_skip_reason.description: The skipped ones, by skip reason.

in_human_pause.description: How many wait in a Human pause.

pending.description: How many wait to be fetched.

its handler and its Payload, and how it is sent and identified.

Whether it goes ahead of every request its domain holds pending,

Its identity in the Frontier, declared by the program in place of

payload.description: The data the program attaches for its handler.

priority.description:
Its priority among the requests of its domain: higher goes first,
and a priority never orders requests of different domains (ADR
0004); 0 by default.

oneOf.description: The machine's or the container's memory.

run_id.description: The Run, when one was stopped or refused.

RouteAbortParams.description: What `route.abort` takes: the request, and the error its page sees.

route_id.description: The intercepted request, which an answer names.

What the handler replies to `route.handle` once it ended; a failure

RouteId.description:
One intercepted request a route's handler answers, which `route.*`

url.description: Another URL, judged again by the domain policy.

Its headers, as the page sent them, their names in lowercase, as

Its body, in Base64 (RFC 4648, with padding), when it has one: as

RowsField.description:

annoyances.description:

RulesSource.description: Where a version of the Clean-up rules comes from (ADR 0047).

oneOf.description: The part every executable embeds.

The opt-in daily channel.
The Filter lists fetched from their authors' URLs.

differences.description: Each input that differs from the Run's.

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

A sitemap seed (ADRs 0093 and 0120; CO-10): `sitemap` names a sitemap,
or a site's robots.txt (its path `/robots.txt`), whose `Sitemap:` lines
are read. The engine reads it, and every sitemap index it nests, once
the Run is running, through the domain policy, Politeness and robots.txt,
running no handler; each entry is checked as an enqueue is, at depth 0,
with the Label of the first rule whose pattern matches its URL and no
Payload, and one no rule matches is not added, with `no_rule`. The seed
widens the crawl's scope by the host of the URL it names, and an entry
outside the scope is not added, with `out_of_scope`, so a robots.txt
seed admits its own host's entries from a sitemap on another host it
names, and no other host's.

max_staged_enqueues.description: How many admissions one attempt may stage before it commits: its enqueues, `enqueueLinks` calls and seeds added through `ctx.run`, each held in the engine's memory with the attempt until its commit or its discard. One more fails with `staging_full`, and nothing is staged. 10,000 by default.

max_url_length.description: The longest URL a crawl admits, in characters as the WHATWG parser serializes it, without its fragment (Scrapy's `URLLENGTH_LIMIT`): a longer one is not added, with `max_url_length`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 2,083 by default; `null` turns the cap off.

max_size.description: The longest a crawl request's Payload may be, in bytes of its JSON as the engine writes it, compactly: a longer one is refused at its enqueue with `payload_invalid`, whose `limit` names this setting, since a Payload lives in the Frontier and in every Checkpoint. Large content goes to the Key-value store, and the Payload carries its key. 64 KiB (65,536 bytes) by default.

max.description: How many times a work item whose attempt failed retryably is tried again: 2, Scrapy's `RETRY_TIMES`.

sample_pages.description: How many pages the sample crawl visits.

drain_grace.description: How long `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, drains on `SIGTERM` before it exits: 110 seconds, below the 120-second `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of the Helm chart, which must exceed it. Each run that reaches its next safe point in that time stops with a Checkpoint, resumable by its Run ID; one that does not stays resumable from its run file. Any Daemon whose listener is closed for good drains the same way within it, then exits 1. An Attached engine that stops on a panic in a part every run shares waits as long for its runs to stop, leaving each one not stopped resumable from its run file, then exits 1. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_DRAIN_GRACE` in milliseconds.

max_rows.description: The most rows one `dataset.query` returns; the rest are counted in its `total`, not returned. 10,000 by default.

memory_limit.description: The most memory, in bytes, one `dataset.query` may use; past it, the query fails with `query_memory_exceeded`. 512 MiB (536870912) by default.

max_size.description: The most bytes of JSON an Effect's body may return for the Effect journal to keep (ADR 0106), 64 KiB by default as `crawl.payload.max_size`. A larger value is `effect_output_invalid` when nothing was sent, and leaves the Effect uncertain after a send.

indent.description: How many spaces a JSON Export indents each level by: 0, the default, writes the array and each Record's value on one line, as committed; 1 to 8 write the array one value per line and each value's members on lines of their own, indented by that many spaces per level. JSONL is one line per Record either way. A count above 8 fails the Export with `setting_invalid`. Set for the connection or the Run.

max_percent.description: The most hedges a run sends, as a whole percentage of the crawl requests its HTTP tier sent: 5 by default.

max.description: How many redirects a crawl request's fetch follows, a refresh stub's hop counted as one: 19 by default, as many as the browser follows in a navigation, from 1 to 19; any other value is refused with `setting_invalid` when the crawl starts. One more fails the request with `too_many_redirects`, so a redirect loop costs a site this many requests and one more. To hand a redirect to the handler unfollowed, list its status in `crawl.handle_statuses`.

max_delay.description: The longest delay of a refresh stub a crawl request's fetch follows: a `Refresh` header, or a `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` outside `<noscript>`, to another URL with a delay up to this is followed at once as one more hop, counted in `fetch.redirect.max`. 100 s by default; `0` follows instant refreshes only, and `null` any delay. A refresh with no URL or to the document's own is never followed.

count.description: How many of a Label's first requests on a domain are samples under `fetch.tier: auto`, each fetched on `http` and then on `browser`, whose run commits, from two Sessions that share nothing where `fetch.http_from` sends the Label's HTTP from the transport, and under `fetch.http_from: learned`, where its `http` run differed, once more on `browser_fetch` from the hop page of the browser run's Session: the Label moves to `http` once all of them gave the same Records and enqueues, and to `browser_fetch` under `learned` once every sample matched there or over `http`. 3 by default; set for the Run only. Fewer than 3 is a weakened control, named in the Run report's `weakened`.

host_cache.description: How many hosts' Clean-up rules this Run keeps built: 1,024, the least used dropped first, and none once the Resource governor finds memory critical. A page on a host it keeps builds no rule list. 0 builds each page's rule list, as before.

contexts_per_process.description: How many of a Run's Sessions share one browser process, each in a browser context of its own: 8. The Run's next Session past it gets a process of its own; Sessions of different Runs never share one.

memory_cap.description: The memory, in bytes, of a browser and its processes past which it is recycled; unset by default, when the cap is twice what the browser used once it had opened its first page.

page_memory_cap.description: The memory, in bytes, of one page's JavaScript heap and the buffers it holds, past which the Resource governor ends the page while memory is critical: 1 GiB. The page ends at its safe point, once no call on it is in flight, and its calls raise `page_memory_exceeded`, which is retryable.

recycle_idle.description: How long a browser may hold no open page before it closes, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage for the browser that replaces it: 5 minutes.

recycle_pages.description: How many pages a browser opens before it is recycled: 100. Recycled, it opens no new page, closes once its pages are done and is replaced, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage.

ceiling.description: The most browser pages the engine's Resource governor admits open at once, across its Runs: 32.

floor.description: The fewest browser pages the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.browser_page.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.

critical.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine's memory is critical: 95.

ceiling.description: The most HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 200.

floor.description: The fewest HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.http.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.

last_resort_after.description: How long the engine's memory may stay critical with its concurrency at the floor before the Resource governor reaches its last resort, when a Daemon's `/readyz` fails: 60 s.

memory_allowance.description: The most memory, in bytes, the engine and its children may use, as its Memory allowance when it is tighter than the process's own cgroup limit, its Windows Job object's limit or half of physical memory; unset by default. Each sample reads it from the engine's settings: the engine's own write (`config.user_write`, `config.policy_write`) is seen at the next sample, a hand edit at the engine's next read of the file, by the next Run's start at the latest.

ceiling.description: The most model calls the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 16.

floor.description: The fewest model calls the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.model_call.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.

pressure.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine is under pressure and its Resource governor lowers its concurrency; also the CPU and Tokio workers' busy share from which they hold it: 85.

run_share.description: The share, in percent, of each kind's concurrency one Run may hold at once, at least one: 100. An Operator policy cap bounds every Run's share.

sample_interval.description: How often the engine's Resource governor reads memory, CPU and Tokio saturation, sizes its concurrency and sends `engine.system_info`: every second.

max_files.description: How many log files an engine process keeps where `log.output` is `file`, the one it writes included: 5, so a Daemon's logs stay under about 50 MiB. The oldest goes at each rotation. A process other than the Daemon writes a set of files of its own, and at its start keeps as many of its executable's sets, its own included, the ones written last. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

max_size.description: The size, in bytes, at which an engine process's log file rotates where `log.output` is `file`: 10 MiB. A file holds at most this much and one line more. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

max_body_size.description: The most decoded bytes of one body the engine itself reads: a page `request`'s response, a kept response, an Operator-configured endpoint's reply. Never a download, which the disk governor bounds. 64 MiB (67108864) by default; set for a connection or a Run. A longer body fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.

max_decompression_ratio.description: The most decoded bytes per received byte of a body the engine reads, once its decoded bytes pass 1 MiB, so a decompression bomb is stopped as it expands. 100 by default; set for a connection or a Run. A body past it fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.

max_hello_size.description: The most bytes of one line a Connection to a listener that takes a token may send before its `hello` is accepted, up to the 16 MiB (16777216) of any message: 64 KiB (65536) by default, many times any `hello`. A longer line closes the Connection unanswered as soon as it passes the limit, without being decoded, and the refusal is logged and recorded as `hello_too_large`. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

max_json_depth.description: The deepest nesting of arrays and objects in JSON the engine parses from outside, from 0 to 1024: 128 by default; set for a connection or a Run. Deeper JSON fails the call with `response_limit_exceeded`.

initial.description: The shortest wait of a domain's backoff: each wait is drawn at random between it and three times the previous wait (the first between it and three times it), never above `politeness.backoff.max`: 2 s. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.

max.description: The longest wait of a domain's backoff: 60 s. A `Retry-After` may hold the domain longer, up to `politeness.retry_after.max`. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.

burst.description: How many crawl requests may start at once on one domain key under `politeness.domain.rate`, the size of its token bucket: 1 by default, so the starts are spread evenly over the minute. A value of 0 is read as 1.

concurrency.description: How many requests may be in flight at once on one domain key, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness: a run admits one only while that combined count is below its own value. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1. A value above 1 is listed in the run's result as one that presses a site harder.

delay.description: How long a run waits after the last request start on a domain key, by any run of the user that shares Politeness, before it starts another there. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1 s. A value below 1 s is listed in the run's result as one that presses a site harder.

rate.description: How many crawl requests a minute may start on one domain key, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, as a token bucket of `politeness.domain.burst` tokens refilled at this rate: 30 holds a site to 30 requests a minute. Each run is held to its own value; the delay between starts still applies. None by default.

concurrency.description: How many page navigations may be in flight at once through one proxy endpoint and credential, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, each redirect hop of a page's main frame counted, a program's own navigation included (a page's other requests and `page.request` are not counted): a run sends one only while that combined count is below its own value and below the ceiling the proxy's own refusals taught. At least 1; none by default, for no cap.

rate.description: How many page navigations a second may start through one proxy endpoint and credential, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness, each redirect hop of a page's main frame counted, a program's own navigation included (a page's other requests and `page.request` are not counted): a run starts one only once a second divided by its own value has passed since the last start there by any sharing run. None by default.

max.description: The longest a crawl waits for the time a site's `Retry-After` asks, past `politeness.backoff.max`: 15 minutes. When the site asks for longer, nothing is sent to its domain before that time and nothing waits for it: the request whose response asked, and each request admitted to the domain meanwhile, ends `failed` with `response_unavailable`, and `run.retry_failed` re-admits them once the site is back. Whatever its value, nothing is sent sooner than the site asked.

sticky_lifetime.description: How long, in milliseconds, a Session asks its provider to keep its proxy exit: the provider's longest when unset. A Session that outlives it is named by the Run report's `proxy_exit_may_change` warning; the engine never looks the exit up. A `list` server's exit never changes.

attempt_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.

resolution_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.

commit_interval.description: How often `run_state.batch.sync: interval` syncs a batch, and an idle Run's last changes.

budget.description: The most memory this Run's Frontier, Leases and changes not yet written may hold, in bytes. Past it, or under memory pressure, state already written leaves memory and is read back from the run file. 0 keeps the Frontier in the run file. A budget of 0 with `run_state.batch.pages`, `.interval` and `.bytes` all `none` is refused, since nothing would ever leave memory.

echo_repeats.description: How many times the sample operation repeats a text.

max_age.description: How long after it opened a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3,000 s, Crawlee's `maxAgeSecs`.

max_error_score.description: The error score at which a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3. A block or a failed Page check adds 1, a success takes 0.5 off, never below 0 (Crawlee's model).

max_size.description: How many Sessions a crawl's Session pool keeps open at once, whether each sends from its own HTTP transport or from its browser: 100. A request goes to an open Session of the client it needs at its domain's proxy tier that has room under `session.pool.session_concurrency`, a new Session opening only when none has room and the pool is under this size; a full pool draws among the busy ones.

max_uses.description: How many requests one Session of a crawl's Session pool serves before it is retired: 50, Crawlee's `maxUsageCount`.

session_concurrency.description: How many requests one Session of a crawl's Session pool serves at once under `session.pool.growth: on_demand`: 1. Unset, a Session serves any number, so the pool opens one Session for each client and proxy tier.

max_crawl_delay.description: The longest robots.txt Crawl-delay a crawl waits out between request starts on a domain key while `site_preferences.respect_robots_txt` is on: 30 s. A host asking for more has its crawl requests skipped with `crawl_delay`, and its delay is not raised.

critical_free.description: The free space, in bytes, below which a filesystem a Run writes to is at the `critical` storage level: every Run with an essential write on it stops resumably at its next safe point, with `resource: "storage"`, and a new Run whose run file would go there is refused with `resources_exhausted`. Unset, each filesystem takes the smaller of 1 GiB and 2 % of its size, and free inodes go by 2 %; `0` turns the level off, which the Run's report lists in `weakened`. Each sample of the Resource governor reads it from the engine's settings: the engine's own write (`config.user_write`, `config.policy_write`) is seen at the next sample, a hand edit at the engine's next read of the file, by the next Run's start at the latest; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

low_free.description: The free space, in bytes, below which a filesystem a Run writes to is at the `low` storage level: its Runs go on, record no Run trace video, store no new Response cache entry, skip their periodic Checkpoints onto it, and carry the warning `storage_low`. Unset, each filesystem takes the smaller of 5 GiB and 10 % of its size, and free inodes go by 10 %; `0` turns the level off, which the Run's report lists in `weakened`. Each sample of the Resource governor reads it from the engine's settings: the engine's own write (`config.user_write`, `config.policy_write`) is seen at the next sample, a hand edit at the engine's next read of the file, by the next Run's start at the latest; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

action.description: How long a locator action waits for its target to be unique and actionable, and replays a gesture that landed elsewhere, before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, or `target_not_unique` for a target still ambiguous: 30 s.

agent.description: How long an Agent's task may run, its actions and model calls nested inside, before it stops with `ended: stopped` and the reason `timeout`: 10 min.

ai.description: How long an AI verb may take from its call to its return, its model calls and a Repair included, before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 120 s.

close.description: One bound for a stop of a Run: how long `run.stop` or a scope's close waits for its next safe point before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, the Run still stopping there, and how long that safe point then waits for each running Effect body's `effect.close` before it cuts the body short, in a drain no later than half of `daemon.drain_grace` from the drain's start: 30 s.

connect.description: How long `connect()` and the CLI wait for the engine to answer `hello` before they fail with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s. Set only in the project file, which they read before they connect; a connection's own is `connect()`'s `timeout`.

dataset_query.description: How long one `dataset.query` may run before it is stopped and fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

first_byte.description: How long a request may wait for its response's first byte before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

handler.description: How long a crawl's handler has for one attempt, which also bounds every action inside it, and from which a work item's lease is derived: the timeout plus the larger of 10 s and a tenth of it. 60 s, Crawlee's `requestHandlerTimeoutSecs`.

hello.description: How long a Connection to a listener that takes a token, a Daemon's or an Attached engine's private endpoint, may take to send its complete `hello`, from its accept: 5 s. One that has not by then is closed unanswered, and the refusal logged and recorded as `hello_timed_out`. An Attached engine's stdio takes no token and has no such deadline. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

hook.description: How long each call of a Hook may run before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 10 s. A crawl's Label may set it for the Hooks on its requests.

human_pause.description: How long a Human pause may wait for a person before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 24 h; in a scheduled run, ADR 0036's pause timeout governs too, and the first to expire acts.

launch.description: How long a browser the engine launches, or a Borrowed one it connects to, may leave each command of its bring-up unanswered, its identity read's page load included, before the call that needs it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.

model.description: How long one attempt of one model request may take before it is retried within the call that made it: 60 s.

navigation.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.

run.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.

secret.description: How long a Secret provider may take to answer one reference before the resolution fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "timed_out"`: 30 s. A provider that answers it is briefly busy, such as a rate limit's, is asked again within it, with exponential backoff and full jitter, after its `Retry-After` when it gave one.

sink_write.description: How long one write to a Sink may take before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

wait.description: How long a wait for an application state, such as `page.wait_for_request_finished`, may take before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

ledger_read_interval.description: How long a going Run charges on the Limits it holds before it reads them again from the Usage ledger for the changes an engine of another process made, such as a `usage set` through a Daemon while an SDK's engine crawls: 1000 ms. A change made by an engine of the Run's own process reaches its next charge, and a Run reads them again before each Slice it takes, so a Limit another process sets reaches a going Run at its next Slice or within this long, whichever comes first. A charge its Slices cover reads nothing in between: no SQL statement and no file operation. `0` reads them at every charge, one ledger read per charge. A Run reads it as it opens; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

lock.description: The values it sets and locks: no higher layer changes them.

max_requests_per_minute.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset.

otlp.description: Whether an engine process also sends each new Audit log entry, the hash with it, as an OpenTelemetry event to the OTLP/HTTP collector `otlp.logs_endpoint` names: off by default, and nothing is sent while `otlp.logs_endpoint` is unset. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

refusals_per_minute.description: How many of one listener's refusals the Audit log records in a minute, from its first: 10. Each refusal past them is still logged, and once the minute ends one `endpoint_refusals_folded` entry counts them, so a peer that retries a wrong token cannot make the engine write an entry per attempt. 0 records none but the counts. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

retention.description: How long the user's Audit log keeps an entry, in milliseconds, such as 15552000000 for the six months the EU AI Act asks of high-risk deployers. Unset, the default, nothing is ever pruned. Set, the engine prunes the entries older than it as it starts and then once a day, so an entry may stay up to a day longer, from the log's beginning only, leaving an anchor entry that carries the last pruned hash, from which `audit verify` checks the rest, and a pruning record at the tail. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

access_mode.description: The Access mode a Session opens in and keeps for its life: `standard` (the default), the browser's own identity; `identified`, which declares who the program is, signing each request it sends with `identified.signing_key` (Web Bot Auth), and masks nothing; or `stealth`, which turns on the whole stealth catalog, each `stealth.*` item of which can be switched off. A non-`none` `stealth.fingerprint_method` makes the Session `stealth`; an explicit `standard` or `identified` beside one at the same scope is `setting_invalid` naming both keys. A stealth item set explicitly where a `standard` Session opens is `setting_not_applicable`, and one set explicitly on an `identified` Session is `setting_invalid` naming both keys; an inherited one yields, which `config explain` names in the item's `yields_to`. `stealth` on WebKit is `capability_unavailable`; a Borrowed browser stays `standard` with its own identity, and `stealth` set where one opens is `setting_not_applicable`, as is `identified` at an import or on a Profile directory used in place. Changing the mode, the Identity profile or the proxy means opening a new Session. A Label refuses it with `setting_not_applicable`.

block_resources.description: The resource kinds the Session's pages never load, failed as `BlockedByClient` by its interception before every navigation: any of `image`, `media`, `font` and `stylesheet`; none by default. The never-block list still loads a challenge's own. In `standard` and `stealth` the Run warns once per Session that the site can see the missing loads.

cdp_command_log.description: Whether the Run trace keeps its CDP command log, `trace/cdp-commands.jsonl`: one line for each command the engine sends a Session's browser, its method only, never its params, up to the launch's last `Browser.close`. Off by default: no command's method goes to the Run trace's writer and the file is never written. Turn it on to see every command the engine sent, such as to debug a Run. No result, Record or Provenance entry reads the log, so off weakens no guarantee.

headless.description: Whether the Session's Chromium runs with no window: `true` by default. Headless or not, the site sees one browser's identity, with no `HeadlessChrome` token in its user agent, except under `browser.headless_shell`.

headless_shell.description: Whether the Session's Chromium is Chrome for Testing's `chrome-headless-shell` build, of the same pinned release, in place of the full browser: `false` by default. The shell runs only headless and differs from the full browser in fingerprint and features: a site sees its own identity, `HeadlessChrome` in its user agent and client hints, where the full build shows its window's. It starts where the full browser's headless mode cannot, such as on macOS with no GUI session (`browser_needs_gui_session`). It is downloaded on first use, as the full build is. Refused with `setting_not_applicable` beside `browser.headless: false`, and under the `stealth` Access mode, which launches its own build; a Borrowed browser launches nothing, so it takes no effect there.

mirror.description: The URL a missing Chrome for Testing build is downloaded below, each build at `<build>/<platform>/<archive>-<platform>.zip` as Chrome for Testing lays them out: Chrome for Testing's own storage by default, or a mirror of it, whose certificate may chain to the authorities `tls.trusted_cas` lists for its domain. A mirror is an Operator-configured endpoint: `egress.no_private_endpoints` refuses one on a private address. What it sends is still checked against the pinned digest. Only Operator policy and user and project configuration set it: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`.

service_workers.description: Whether a site's service workers run in the Session's pages: `allow` (the default on Chromium) runs them under the Session's interception, each worker's own requests passing the domain policy, the Filter lists and the Session's routes, never a page's routes; `block` makes `navigator.serviceWorker.register()` reject as on a failed fetch of the worker's script, `register` staying the browser's own function, so that every request of a page reaches its routes.

max_unused_age.description: How long a Pinned artifact no installed executable pins stays in the Browser cache unused before the clean-up deletes it, and how long an executable's entry counts as installed after it was last seen: 30 days. `null` turns the automatic clean-up off. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

read_only.description: Whether a Run's Chromium launches only read the Browser cache: `false` by default. When on, a build with its pinned digest is launched with no use recorded, a build of the wrong digest is refused with `browser_not_installed` and left in place, and a missing build is never downloaded: `artifact_unavailable_offline` under `egress.offline`, `browser_not_installed` otherwise. The engine then writes no file of its own in the cache, its write check's included; the browser still writes in its build's files as it does at every launch. Each Product's testing kit turns it on, so a test leaves the caller's cache as it found it.

interval.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.

channel.description: The OCI repository the daily channel is pulled from, `host[:port]/path`: Goodfetch's own on ghcr.io by default, or a mirror of it, which `clean_up.update = daily` makes the configured destination. Only Operator policy and user and project configuration set it: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`.

fetch_timeout.description: How long fetching a version of the Clean-up rules from its sources may take at a Run's start or resume: past it, a Run holds to the newest version this machine has, and a `clean_up.version` it cannot fetch refuses the start. 30 s.

lists.description: The URL `clean_up.update = upstream` fetches each Filter list from, by list: `ads` (EasyList), `trackers` (EasyPrivacy), `annoyances` (Fanboy Annoyance) and `unbreak` (Brave's unbreak list); their authors' own URLs by default, or a mirror's. Each must be `https`. Only Operator policy and user and project configuration set it: a Recipe's or a run's value is `setting_locked`.

update.description: Where a new Run's Clean-up rules come from: `release` (the default), the set this release pins, with the embedded part as fallback; `daily`, the opt-in daily channel, whose registry it makes a configured destination, refused with `capability_unavailable` until the engine checks the channel's signature; `upstream`, the Filter lists from their authors' URLs, which it makes configured destinations. A Run holds to the version it starts with for its whole life, a resume included; `egress.offline` turns the fetching off. Operator policy can lock it.

version.description: The exact version of the Clean-up rules a new Run holds to, by its digest `sha256:<hex>` as Provenance names it, instead of the newest one `clean_up.update` gives: a daily version it names is fetched from the daily channel, and it is exempt from the channel's expiry and its refusal of older versions. None by default.

max_listener_queue.description: The most events the Client holds for one listener that has not taken them yet, a whole number from 1: 1024 by default. Past it the listener loses the events that follow; once it has taken those it held, it is removed and ends with `listener_events_lost` naming how many it lost, and the other listeners go on. The TypeScript Client applies it to its own transport. Set in `connect()`'s own `settings` only.

max_pending_calls.description: The most calls the Client holds waiting for their answer, a whole number from 1: 10000 by default. A call past it is refused at once, unsent, with `connection_overloaded` and the bound `pending_calls`; the calls made before it go on. The TypeScript, Python and Rust Clients apply it to their own transport from their first call, `hello` included. Set in `connect()`'s own `settings` only.

max_queued_write_bytes.description: The most bytes the Client holds waiting to be written to the engine, a whole number from 1: 64 MiB (67108864) by default. While bytes wait, a call whose message would pass it is refused at once, unsent, with `connection_overloaded` and the bound `queued_write_bytes`; the calls made before it go on, and one message larger than the bound is still taken while nothing waits. The TypeScript, Python and Rust Clients apply it to their own transport from their first call, `hello` included. Set in `connect()`'s own `settings` only.

domains.description: The registrable domains on which a run accepts a consent wall, a Consent prompt with no refusal that covers the content or offers payment instead, rather than raising `blocked` with `consent_required`; `*` only when written. A prompt that offers a refusal is still refused there. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer.

handling.description: What a browser Session does with Consent prompts: `answer` (the default, in every Access mode) refuses each prompt in every frame and hides one with no refusal that leaves the content readable; `detect` only looks: nothing is clicked or hidden, the wall test still runs, and a consent wall is still `consent_required`; `off` registers and starts no Consent prompt runner and lets no cosmetic rule act on the live page or in extracted content, so no consent wall is reported and the page's text is returned as served, while the Filter lists still block requests; the Run report lists `off` in `weakened`. A Recipe, and a Client acting for a model, never set `off` unless the layers below already give it: `setting_locked`; set it in the program's own code, in configuration or in an Operator policy.

on_wall.description: What a consent wall on a domain outside `consent.domains` does: `report` (the default) leaves the page at `consent_required`, raised as `blocked`; `ask` raises a Human pause for a person's answer, for this run or always for the domain. Until the Human pause takes a person's answer, `ask` opens no page: `capability_unavailable`.

extractor.description: The main-content step `page.formats` reads a page's main content with, before its Markdown, its main HTML and its text: `dom_smoothie` (the default), Readability's algorithm, or `trafilatura`, the rs-trafilatura port. A step that finds no text in a document holding text outside its navigation landmarks answers that text. Set at any scope down to a page: a Run, a Session's or a page's own `settings`.

content_types.description: The media types a Label's handler takes, each `type/subtype`, `type/*` or `*/*`, set for the Run or for one of its Labels, whose own list wins for its requests: `text/html` and `application/xhtml+xml` by default. A response that would reach the handler (a 2xx, or a status `crawl.handle_statuses` lists) of another type ends its request `skipped` with the reason `content_type` before its body is read, never retried. The type is the response's `Content-Type` essence, or, when it names none, the type the pinned Chromium's MIME sniffer gives its first 1,024 bytes; a response with neither a type nor a body is an empty HTML document. An accepted type that is not HTML or XHTML reaches the handler with its body in its response and a page holding no document, whose document calls fail with `response_not_document`. A handler's own navigations are not checked. A value that is no list of media ranges is refused with `setting_invalid` when the crawl starts.

domain_keys.description: Host names, each with the domain key its requests and those of the hosts under it share, the longest name winning, in place of the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List: a Recipe's override of the key its per-domain queues use. None by default.

domain_order.description: Which ready site gets the next free request slot. `fewest_in_flight` picks the site with the fewest of this Run's requests in flight, so a slow site never holds every slot. `round_robin` takes each ready site in turn, one request each.
